Invisible on a couch (only the head shows) and at a desk; ruinous on a profile seat. ⛔⛔⛔ **A `vw`/`vh` LENGTH INSIDE THE TEXT SIZE BODY ZOOM IS NOT A FIT CAP ABOVE 100% — IT IS THE OVERFLOW.** The unit resolves against the REAL viewport and is THEN multiplied by the zoom, so `.mkt`'s `max-height: 92vh` rendered as **133vh** at HUGE. Measured live at 1440×900, the bay's box against the real glass: **100% 1180×828 fits · 115% 1357×952 (±26) · 130% 1440×1076 (±88) · 145% 1440×1201 (±150)** — the scrim centres, so the excess splits top AND bottom and takes the ✕ with it (**top:-4 / -63 / -122**). The only mouse way out of a modal sat OFF the glass: the bay could not be used or closed without going back to STANDARD first. **115% is what AUTO picks on a ≤1470px screen, so this was the DEFAULT on a laptop.** The COMMS lightbox carried the identical cap (measured ±5 / ±65 / ±124 with an oversized image).

⛔⛔ **A FRAME GETS ONE OF TWO TREATMENTS, AND `%` IS THE BETTER ONE.** A child of a `position:fixed; inset:0` layer (a scrim, `.screen`) sizes off it with a PERCENTAGE — that layer is **viewport-exact under zoom (probed: 1440×900 at every scale)**, so % of it IS the glass in the frame's own zoomed frame, with no reciprocal to forget: `.mkt`, `.comms-lightbox .lb-frame` + its image + caption, `.connect-panel`. A body-level fixed panel with nothing to be a percentage of carries the `--sn-unzoom` reciprocal like `.term` already did: `.fnv-floating`, `#boot-inner`, `.pw`, `.tut-coach.kit`. Those four were **dead guards, not overflows** — their `vw` caps could never bind under zoom, so they protected nothing on a narrow frame.

⛔⛔ **AN IMAGE CAP INSIDE A `%`-SIZED FLEX FRAME IS `min-height: 0`, NOT A SECOND VIEWPORT CAP.** A percentage height cannot resolve against a content-sized parent, so `.lb-frame img`'s old `calc(88vh - 28px)` has no `%` equivalent — the honest fix is to let the image ride flex-shrink (`min-height:0` defeats a flex item's content-based minimum) inside the frame's own cap, which also keeps the caption's row counted.

⛔⛔ **THE `.term` FAMILY WAS NEVER BROKEN, AND MY FIRST PROBE SAID IT WAS.** An early sweep reported right-edge overflow on all 11 windows at 115/130% — it measured synchronously after `openTerm`, i.e. **before the rAF `fitTermInViewport` clamp ran and mid `term-power` (heights read `3px`)**. Waiting 700ms turned 23 "failures" into 0. **Finish the animation AND let the clamp's rAF fire before believing any window rect** — and open windows ONE AT A TIME, because the 2nd+ cascade +32px and read as drift.

⛔ **A CSS FIT BUG IS INVISIBLE IN A SCREENSHOT AND OBVIOUS IN A RECT SWEEP.** The proof here is a CDP probe that opens every surface at {100,115,130,145}% at two window sizes (1440×900 and 1280×800) and reports `overTop/overBottom/overLeft/overRight` plus whether the ✕ is on the glass: bay both tabs, lightbox with a 3000×3000 image, floating dialogue, and all 12 dock windows enumerated LIVE from `[data-term]` rather than hardcoded — **0 overflowing measurements after the fix**. `textsize-screen-space.test` now carries the standing rule; reverting `.mkt` to its old values reddens it on exactly those two declarations.

Measured over a full cycle at 1440×900, share of frame carrying gas: **tile 1366 `0.060–0.208` · tile 1920 `0.043–0.350` · tile 2048 `0.043–0.396`** — i.e. many minutes at a stretch of stars and nothing else, which is exactly the frame Andrew screenshotted.

**THE FIX IS FRAMING, NOT SLOWING.** `build()` records the cloud's centre from the half-res density field `fT`; `draw()` pins that centre to the centre of the frame and SWAYS about it (two out-of-phase waves, peak speeds ~1.2 and ~0.3 px/s — the *same* rates the old drift ran at, so the motion reads unchanged; it just stops accumulating). Camera parallax at `D.gas` is untouched, so law 2 still holds and panning still slides the field; the foreground motes keep their own drift. ⛔⛔ **A FIXED TILE IS A TORUS, SO THE PLAIN CENTROID OF ITS CONTENT IS MEANINGLESS.** A cloud straddling the wrap seam has its linear centroid in the empty middle — the pin would have framed the hole. The centre is the **circular mean**: read each axis as an angle, sum density as unit vectors, convert the resultant angle back. The resultant LENGTH is kept as `focus.r` and `draw()` falls back to the unpinned offset below `0.08`, so a future tune that spreads the gas evenly degrades to the old behaviour instead of pinning to a meaningless point.

Andrew, on a screenshot of a live `/steer` landing mid-run: *"when it says 'steering' it appears to have its own separate glowing square right under it, and then under that u have the glowing WORKING square. whenever its steering I dont want it to have its own glowing square."*

⛔⛔ **A SIDECAR EVENT THAT IS NOT THE AGENT'S PROSE MUST NOT RIDE THE PROSE PATH.** `sidecar/loop.js` surfaces a folded steering note by emitting it as an `agent.token` delta (`'\n[steering] ' + t + '\n'`) — deliberately, so the Commander SEES their steer land — but `streamingAgent()` treats every token as agent prose, so the Commander's own words opened a caret'd paragraph and blinked a ▮ as if the model were typing them. Two blinking squares stacked (the steer's caret + the WORKING chip) is the visible symptom; the real fault is **attribution**: the transcript was performing the human's note as machine output. Fixed in `streamingAgent.append` — a delta matching `[steering] <line>` closes the open paragraph and renders as its own `.cmsg.tool.steer-echo` note row (no caret), and the prose around it keeps streaming normally. The split is capture-aware (`split(/(?:^|\n)\[steering\] ([^\n]*)\n?/)`), so a note arriving in the SAME delta as surrounding prose still separates cleanly.

⛔ **THE TWO "MULTIPLE CHOICE" SURFACES ARE DIFFERENT SYSTEMS — do not conflate them when a report names one.** The chip path (`Chat.choices`, onboarding V3 §3/S1 steering chips) never answers on its own and opens the typed path; the path in this report is the free-text `/steer` command → `POST /api/run/steer` → the loop's mid-run fold. Only the latter emits the `[steering]` token echo. A fix aimed at the chips would have touched nothing Andrew was looking at.

⛔ **A `frontend/app/*.js` EDIT OWES `npm run sync:website` OR THE GATE DIES 231 STEPS IN.** `test/run-recovery-ui.test.js` byte-compares `website/app/app/chat.js` against the frontend original, and its failure prints the ENTIRE expected file (~1.1MB) — the diff is invisible in the noise, so read `run-fast-tests: FAILED at step N/630` and regenerate rather than trying to read the assertion. The accent is not lost and not decoration: **it is the SUIT the agent wears on the floor** (a painted object, any colour is fine), and the builder's swatch now says so. Class identity stays where `classicons.js` always put it — the emblem SHAPE and the 3-letter code, never the colour.

They collided too: **43 distinct marks across 91 recipes, ◐ on five different ones.** Fixed with one engraved seal per CATEGORY as `svg()`'s fallback — measured after: **101/101 built-ins resolve real vector art**; a CUSTOM recipe still shows its author's emoji.

Andrew, circling a station corner twice: *"the wall texture as it curves doesnt connect to the next wall ... it just continues on and gets cut off"*, then *"what are these weird flap things on the edges?"*, then *"can you fill in the the textures"*. Four distinct defects, one family — every one of them a corner asserting a surface it has no right to.

⛔⛔⛔ **A DEPTH MEASURE THAT OUTLIVES ITS PROFILE PAINTS A FLAT SLAB.** Past the ring's centre line the outline is the constant straight-run offset, but `faceMap` kept measuring depth RADIALLY from the LIFTED arc centre — so on a top corner, walking DOWN the column moves AWAY from that centre, the radius grows, and depth SHRINKS to 0 and clamps. Every clamped pixel samples the same strip row, so a 22px standing face against a 13px profile rendered as one repeated row: the "triangle". **A flat-colour run inside a textured pass IS a clamped coordinate** — census the column, count the repeats. Fix: depth down a standing face is a ROW COUNT, not a radius (along = world x, depth = rows under the crown — what `bakeTallNorthFace` shows on the wall beside it). Bottom corners keep the polar measure: `cy === ay` there, the face is short, and the concentric bands are the point of the curve.

⛔⛔⛔ **THE TALL NORTH FACE IS 28px AND A TWO-TILE ALLEY IS 24px — SO A WALL REACHES INTO THE TILE BEHIND IT.** Where footprints sit a tile or two apart both rooms extrude into the sliver between them, and every straight wall is painted before every chamfer, so the FARTHER corner won. It flattened the nearer wall's face under a bright crown bar (the "cut off"), and its deck/foot art bit a dark diagonal out of the nearer wall's crown (the "doesn't blend"). The 2026-08-11 depth law — south paints last — had only ever been applied chamfer-to-chamfer. It now covers corner-vs-STRAIGHT-wall, in `bakeCornerCrown`'s `put` AND in the corner-art pass's `fill` (`clamp` routes through it). Nothing is left unpainted: the nearer wall drew those rows in full, which is exactly why it may keep them.

⛔⛔ **FIXING THE DEPTH EXPOSED A HOLE THE CLAMP HAD BEEN HIDING — AND DELETING BAD PAINT PUNCHED ANOTHER.** Once depth counted correctly the corner reached strip rows it had never sampled, and on a VIEWPORT wall those rows are the GLASS: `stripAt` returns null, the slice skipped, and the window wrapped round the bend with the starfield showing through. **A WINDOW DOES NOT TURN A CORNER** — a corner is solid by construction, so a null sample now falls back to `pal.face`'s ladder (NOT `base`, which carries the glass tone). Separately, simply dropping the bad face slice left black void, because those rows are the lifted ramp ABOVE the wall's own tiles where `bakeSideFace` never reaches. **A null from a texture lookup is not automatically "leave it open" — ask what the transparency MEANS.**

⛔⛔ **I SHIPPED TWO WRONG NUMBERS.** (1) The orphan-tail enumerator scored "is this arm exterior" by stepping the CORNER's diagonal instead of the direction that arm's SIDE faces — one tile off; 6 became 3. (2) It then counted `bl`/`br` corners, which **cannot** orphan: `cornerArcCy` lifts the arc centre for `tl`/`tr` only, so on a bottom corner `t = py + 0.5 - ay` is never ≤ 0 and there is no straight tail; `bl@40,14` was a false positive and cost a hunt for a defect that could not exist. Honest count: **2**, both the corners Andrew circled. **A derived statistic needs its OWN check, not the fix's.**

✅ **ALL 10 WALL RECIPES SWEPT, MEASURED NOT EYEBALLED** (`dev/wallcorner-materials.mjs`): `geo.wallMatOf` is a plain function on the projected geometry, so forcing each recipe needs no shipped-code edit — one boot covers all ten. **0 unpainted pixels for every material at 3 corners** (two lifted top corners + one bottom corner, proving bottom corners did not move). ⛔ The companion `flatRun` metric is NOT a clean detector — its band also covers the crown and any genuinely flat panel; it points you at a crop, it does not decide.

⛔⛔⛔ **"THE FLOORS WON'T BLEND" WAS NEVER A BLEND FAILURE — READ THE USER'S SAVE.** Andrew's station: **eight rooms, not one pair touching.** r5/r6/r7/r8 sit **one tile** off r1, r3 two, r9 three; `seamOpenJoins` reports **0 open joins**. Every "unblended seam" was two separate hulls each correctly drawing its own wall and shell across a gap of void. The same seven rooms placed flush give **72 open joins** and one continuous deck. Two full lanes of seam work (08-06, and this one's first day) were spent looking at the bake for a defect that was in the *placement*. `dev/seamblend-station.mjs` answers this in one command; the screenshot alone had me estimating room widths for hours.

⛔⛔ **A VALIDATOR THAT ONLY REJECTS OVERLAP SILENTLY PERMITS THE NEAR-MISS.** `checkRects` rejects `OVERLAP` and nothing else, so a one-tile gap is a perfectly legal placement — and at `TILE=12` it is a handful of screen pixels, invisible until the bake draws two walls where you expected none. The tool let you miss by one and said nothing. **When "almost right" and "right" are indistinguishable on screen, the gesture owes the user the snap.**

⛔⛔ **TWO GESTURES, TWO SNAP BEHAVIOURS — A CLICK MAY NOT RESIZE.** A CLICK stamps the size the user last drew, so it **translates**; changing that size is taking a decision that isn't ours. A DRAG *is* sizing, so it moves the near **edge** and the room grows to meet its neighbour. MOVE snaps on the bounding box with the delta applied to every rect, so an L-shaped room keeps its shape. Conflating the two would have made click-to-place quietly resize the remembered footprint.

⛔⛔ **A SNAP MUST FACE, VALIDATE, AND STAY BOUNDED.** Offered only when the two footprints' spans overlap on the *other* axis (or a room across the station tugs at a placement it can never touch); every candidate re-validated through the model's own validator (so a snap can never create the overlap it exists to prevent); capped at `SNAP_FIT` = 2 tiles (so a genuinely-nowhere-near aim is placed where you put it, never teleported). Same discipline the LINES tool's `SNAP_R` already used.

⛔⛔ **PROVE A SNAP ON THE GESTURE, NEVER ON THE ARITHMETIC.** Asserting `snapFit()` directly proves the maths and nothing about the half that breaks silently: **the ghost showing flush while the click commits the raw gesture one tile off.** `__test__.placeDrag` drives the real `onDown`/`onMove`/`onUp` with the tool armed, so ghost and commit both go through it, and the proof measures the resulting **gap in tiles** — the user-visible fact. Measured: 1-short east `x19→x18` gap **0**; 2-short east `x20→x18` gap **0** (both axes); 1-short south `y12→y11` gap **0**; 13 tiles away → **untouched**. `rememberDrawn` reads the SNAPPED rect, so a room that grew to meet its neighbour teaches the next click that size.

⛔ **EACH CASE IN A PLACEMENT PROOF MUTATES THE STATION THE NEXT ONE IS TESTED AGAINST.** The first run had every east case in one y band, so case 2 came back `rejected` — for overlapping the room *case 1 had just placed*. That reads exactly like a snap failure and is not one. Space the cases onto their own bands, or rebuild the station per case.

**Together with `3a200cfc7` (hallway corner chamfer) this closes the "rooms and hallways don't join cleanly" arc**: the corner defect was a hallway never being chamfered at all, and the "seam" defect was rooms that were never adjacent. One-line cause, in `worldmodel.js` `projectGeometry`: chamfers were computed for **rooms only** (`if (rm.kind === 'corridor') continue;`). Diff is `worldmodel.js` + `worldmodel.test.js` + the mirror + four dev probes. No sidecar, route, shared-contract, package, credential or external-release change.

⛔⛔⛔ **A HALLWAY'S CORNER WAS NEVER ROUNDED AT ALL.** With no chamfer, a corridor's convex void-exposed corner is a raw right angle where the **tall north face** — extruded up-screen by `WALL.corUp` — meets the **side band**, which is a top surface at *floor level*. Those two live at different heights by construction and nothing reconciled the step, so the corner rendered as a stub with a notch beside it. A room never shows this because a room gets the chamfer. It is also exactly why the defect tracked the 08-08 wall lane: **the height of the step IS `corUp`**, so raising it 8→12 turned a nick into a block.

⛔⛔⛔ **THE EXCLUSION WAS LOAD-BEARING — "corridors stay slim" IS ABOUT WALKABILITY, NOT ART.** A chamfer tile is also an **unwalkable** tile. `MIN_HALL` allows 2 wide, so blocking both corners of a 2-wide end row severs the hallway, and a **2×2 hallway would have all four corners blocked and become an impassable hole** in the station's connectivity — silently, on saves that already exist (Andrew has a 2×2 joining r3→r1). Measured rather than feared: with the block left in, a 2×2 hallway comes back with **2 of its 4 tiles walkable**. The fix is to split two meanings that were only ever conflated — `chamfers` (ART: what the bake rounds, rooms **and** corridors) from `chamferBlock` (WALKABILITY: what stops being floor, rooms only). Corridor walkability is unchanged. **Before deleting a narrowing condition, ask what it was narrowing.**

⛔⛔ **THREE WRONG HYPOTHESES, EACH KILLED BY MEASUREMENT — AND THE USER'S SHAPE WAS NONE OF THEM.** (1) *Corridor-to-room* — built four such cases; all four looked fine and taught nothing, because a corridor's walls are only ever reconciled against a **room's**, never against its own turn. (2) *Two corridors contending for the corner* — split the wall pass so tall north faces draw last; **changed exactly zero pixels**, so the theory died and the change was reverted rather than left in with a comment asserting a mechanism that isn't real. (3) *A missing join pass* — per-corridor pixel attribution returned **0 lost, 0 gained, 725 repainted**, i.e. no join pass exists but nothing is being destroyed either. What actually settled it was Andrew pointing at the angle: it is **one hallway's own NW corner**, not a junction between two.

⛔⛔ **A PROBE MUST STRIP THE FIX TO SHOW A BEFORE, NOT ASSUME ITS ABSENCE.** Once corridor chamfers shipped, `projectGeometry` emits them itself — so the ladder was comparing the fix against itself and returned two identical panels. BEFORE now *filters corridor chamfers back out* (which IS the pre-fix geometry); AFTER takes whatever the shipped path produces and never restates it. Same law the roomshape live harness needed the day before: **a probe that hardcodes what it is testing goes blind to the change.**

⛔⛔ **NEVER TEXT-REWRITE A REPO FILE TO RUN A CAN-FAIL CHECK.** To prove the new test could go red I `-replace`'d the shipped line via PowerShell and then `git checkout --`'d the file — which reverted **the fix along with the probe edit**, and the file had to be rebuilt from scratch. Use `git stash` (or edit the test, not the source). The check itself was worth it and is the reason the 2×2 hazard is a measured number rather than a worry: restoring the old line turns both new assertions red (`expected 0, got 2` and `expected 4, got 2`).

⛔ **`geo.chamfers` IS A PLAIN ARRAY ON THE PROJECTED GEOMETRY** — a probe can add to or filter it between `projectGeometry()` and `StationBake.bake(geo)`, which is how this hypothesis was confirmed with **zero** changes to shipped code before committing to it.

⛔ **AND AGAIN: `projectGeometry` REBASES EVERY TILE BY THE PAD.** A room authored at x0 comes back at x3, so a bake coordinate computed from the tiles you passed in lands a pad's worth of tiles away — no throw, no blank image, a crisp picture of the wrong place. Cost three renders across two lanes. **Read the rects back out of the geometry the bake was handed.**

**Separate, still open (not this lane):** Andrew's 8 rooms sit **1–3 tiles apart** — the classifier finds **0 open joins** — so the "floors won't blend" complaint on that station is two detached hulls with void between, not a seam failure. The same rooms placed flush give **72 open joins** and one continuous deck. The fix is a **placement snap** in the build ghost (`worldmodel.js` rejects only *overlap*; a 1-tile gap is legal and invisible at 12px a tile). `dev/seamblend-station.mjs` renders and measures it.

**2026-08-08 merge digest (ROOMS THAT READ AS ROOMS — WALL HEIGHT, A LAMP GRID, CHAMFERED CORNERS):** `agent/roomshape` → `feat/harness-backend` as merge `fc5c1eae` from snapshot `04884eb6` (code `6d916ea6`, pitch decision `f60c2efd`, dev harnesses `2e3a7cd4`/`67935000`/`895d1da9`, two trunk syncs `76639f4d`/`66d01319`, W0 re-locks `696c5fc4`/`e5774cbb`/`8ea75f60`). Lane and merged-trunk `npm run test:fast` both **591/591 GREEN**; claims planning authority PASS. Three shipped constants moved, each behind a crtlab slider: `WALL.up` 14→22 (+`corUp` 8→12, `capH` 3→4), new `LIGHT.pitch` 8, new `SHAPE.cornerN` 1. No sidecar, route, shared-contract, package, credential, or external-release change — the diff is `stationbake.js` + `crtlab.js`, the website mirror, and dev probes.

⛔⛔ **ONE ROW OF LAMPS IS NOT LIGHTING, IT IS A LIT STRIP.** The lamp count was a bare `/ 7` on room **WIDTH only**, so every room got exactly one row of fixtures pinned `T*1.6` below its north wall — and a lamp's carve reaches `rad*1.4` ≈ 84px ≈ **7 tiles**. Any room deeper than that sat at raw 0.77 ambient below the first row. Measured on an 18×14 hab, deck luma top→bottom: **40 → 17.5, monotonically, with no recovery.** That is the "empty dark tray" read, and no amount of floor material fixes it — it is the same lesson the corridor deck taught three times: *the texture was being asked to do the light's job.* Lamps now grid DOWN the room as well as across it at `LIGHT.pitch`. Row 0 is deliberately unmoved because it is the row the wall-mounted flood hardware is drawn for, and **hardware must keep its light**.

⛔⛔ **PICK A LIGHTING PITCH BY ITS TROUGH, NEVER BY ITS AVERAGE.** Both candidates lit the whole deck; the question is whether a trough exists at all, because a floor lit by a flat wash has nothing but its pattern to show. Measured: **pitch 7 → 3×3 grid, peak 73.2 / trough 46.5** (an evenly lit warehouse); **pitch 8 → 2×2, peak 55.9 / trough 30.6** (distinct pools with real dark between). Shipped 8. ⚠️ **9 and 10 render IDENTICALLY to 8** — row and column counts are *rounded tile divisions*, so the grid only steps at integer boundaries and several adjacent slider values land on the same rank. Expect this dial to feel dead over stretches; that is arithmetic, not a bug.

⛔⛔⛔ **A SILHOUETTE IS THE RIM YOU SEE, NOT THE CUT YOU MADE.** `SHAPE.cornerN` is the superellipse exponent every corner in the station is cut from (2 = the legacy circular fillet, 1 = a 45° chamfer, higher = squarer), applied inside `eachCornerRow` — the ONE raster every curve in the file shares — so only the *crossing function* changes and every concentric layer follows automatically. The first chamfer render came back **pixel-for-pixel convincing as the old fillet**, and the diff probe said 2875 pixels had changed. Cause: the hull's bright 2px outline was this file's **last surviving stroked `arc()`**, and it had agreed with the erase for years only because *a circle looks the same from both sides*. The erase cut a chamfer; the rim drew a fillet on top of it. Rastered off the shared walk now as a connected contour. **When a shape knob appears to do nothing, look for a second painter drawing the same edge from its own maths.**

⛔⛔ **`n === 2` KEEPS THE ORIGINAL `sqrt` WRITTEN OUT, NOT THE GENERAL FORM.** `r*(1-(ady/r)^n)^(1/n)` is algebraically identical at n=2 but differs in the last float bits, and these values go straight into `Math.round` — a 1px corner shift is exactly the silent regression this file's raster discipline exists to prevent. Same rule applied to the interior ellipse's `dxIn`.

⛔ **A PREFLIGHT MARKER MUST KEY ON STRUCTURE, NEVER ON A VALUE THE LANE EXISTS TO TUNE.** `dev/roomshape-serve.mjs` asserted `pitch: 7` / `up: 22` to prove the port served this branch. Tuning pitch to 8 made it announce the wrong branch **while serving the right one** — worse than no check, because a preflight that cries wolf gets ignored and the run it should have caught goes through. It keys on `SHAPE.cornerN` / `lampRows` / `lampCols` now. Sibling defect in the same lane: `dev/roomshape-live.mjs` *restated* the new numbers when restoring the "after" state, so it would have reported `pitch: 7` as current forever after the change; it stashes the shipped objects on boot and restores those bytes.

⛔ **BAKE PIXELS ARE `tile * T`, NOT `(tile - geo.origin) * T`.** `geo.origin` is the world→screen offset the renderer applies; the bake pass computes `X = ccx * T` itself. Subtracting it in a capture harness throws nothing and produces no blank image — it silently crops a **different part of the station**, which is how a corner ladder came back with four plausible, identical panels that were not showing a corner at all. Verify against `geo.W`.

**Probes:** `dev/roomshape-shots.mjs` (before/after + corner ladder + pitch ladder as contact sheets, with peak/trough per pitch), `dev/roomshape-live.mjs` (live before/after re-baked in ONE seeded session, so the comparison is not also comparing two seeds and two window sizes), `dev/roomshape-diff.mjs` (locates where a knob actually moves pixels), `dev/roomshape-serve.mjs` (seeded server that boots past the agent-creation menu; persistent workspace).

**Live proof:** seeded app booted, `World.rebake()` driven between the old and shipped values in the same session, screenshots taken of both; the running page confirmed holding `up:22 / cornerN:1 / pitch:8`. **NOT verified:** the look was judged on the seed fixture's single hab and one 18×14 test hab (the pixel diff did run across a 2-room station). Corridors, multi-room and stacked layouts, and rooms narrower than one lamp pitch have not been swept by eye — the corner work in particular is the class of change that only misbehaves on a multi-room station.

A sliced row reads as BROKEN, not as scrollable, which is exactly how it was reported. The cap is `--crew-cap` now, MEASURED by `leftrail.js` and rounded DOWN to a row boundary: at least `ROWS_MIN` (4) agents whole, past that the historic 40% share so a tall rail shows MORE rather than parking dead black, never so much that SESSIONS drops below `WS_FLOOR`. `flex-shrink` went to **0** — otherwise a long SESSIONS list squeezes the roster back under its own cap and re-opens the same slice. 40% survives only as the no-JS fallback.

⛔ **DON'T SHIP CSS YOU COULDN'T MEASURE.** A `#crew::-webkit-scrollbar` block was added to force a visible "more below" bar and then **removed**: the gutter measured `offsetWidth-clientWidth = 0` both before AND after, because Chromium ignores those pseudos when `scrollbar-width` is set on the same element. **2026-08-07 merge digest (CRT STRENGTH DIAL — FULL / DULLED):** `agent/nocrt` → `feat/harness-backend` as merge `ff66df21` from snapshot `ab7e426e` (code `5f8659e5`, claims re-lock `39242f2a`, mirror `2e715089`, trunk sync `373cb94c` + regenerated surface `30de822c`); lane gate **579/579 GREEN** post-sync, read from the log. Claims authority PASS, 206 locked surface files. Andrew: users reported the CRT *"makes their eyes hurt"*, and the answer had to keep the tube.

⛔⛔⛔ **THE CRT MAY NEVER BE FULLY DISABLED.** The station IS a tube; a switch that turns it off turns the product's identity off. Two intermediate designs were built and rejected before this one: an on/off toggle, then a FULL/SOFT/OFF ladder. **SOFT was rejected because it DELETED the screen-space glass over the panels rather than easing it** — a second disable wearing a gentler name. The shipped dial is two positions, `full` and `dulled`, and DULLED thins the glass; it never removes it. The check that catches the regression is asserting `getComputedStyle(document.body,'::after').display === 'block'` at BOTH positions.

⛔⛔ **"THE CRT HURTS MY EYES" IS ABOUT THE GLASS OVER THE *TEXT*, NOT THE TUBE.** `body::after` (scanlines, z950) is `position:fixed; inset:0` — it lies over every panel, the crew rail and the COMMS transcript, not just the art. At 14px VT323 a 3px pitch puts ~2.6 troughs of up to 0.30 alpha through the body of every glyph. **Contrast was never the problem** — COMMS copy measures 5.7:1, past AA. It is periodic interference at the glyph's own scale, plus the inherited 4px halo softening every stem. Fix the layer, not the colours.

⛔⛔ **PARAMETERISE DEPTH, NEVER GEOMETRY.** The tunables are now `var()`s whose **fallbacks are the shipped numbers**, so FULL is byte-for-byte unchanged and one class holds every override: `body.crt-dull` sets `--scan-shoulder .13→.06`, `--scan-core .30→.14`, `--scan-core-hi .28→.13`, `--page-vignette .42→.24`. Pitch, stop positions and the graded shoulder stay fixed — widening the pitch is what turns a beam into venetian blinds. The prose halo TIGHTENS `4px→2px` rather than going to `none`: the glow is the phosphor, and killing it makes the copy read as flat web text in a pixel-art station.

⛔ **DE-GLOW BY INHERITANCE, NEVER A `*` SWEEP.** `text-shadow` is inherited and the halo comes from the `body` rule, so naming the four prose containers (`#chat-log`, `.term-body`, `#left`, `#bottombar`) is enough — descendants inherit the tighter value while every chip, button and heading declaring its own glow keeps it. No `!important`, no restore list. A blanket sweep would flatten the chrome's identity along with the copy.

✅ **THE BAY SCRIM NEEDED NO RULE.** `--scan-*` sit on `body` and custom properties inherit, so `.mkt-scrim::after` thins automatically — the old "retune `body::after` and the scrim together" law is now held **structurally** instead of by memory.

⛔ **`no-scan` IS THE VERIFICATION FLAG, NOT A FREE HOOK.** `scripts/verify-stars2.mjs` sets it to flatten the feed for star-pixel checks; a settings `toggle()` would remove it out from under a verification run. The dial drives its own `crt-dull` class, and `world.js`/`app.css` carry NO settings hook at all — the station feed's in-canvas CRT answers only to `no-scan`.

**LIVE-PROVEN** by driving the real chips in Settings → APPEARANCE → CRT: scanlines `display:block` at both levels with troughs `0.13/0.30 → 0.06/0.14`, vignette `0.42 → 0.24`, prose halo `4px → 2px`, tube glass present at both, and **feed row-ripple identical (27.968 / 27.968)** — the station is untouched by the dial. Legacy migration verified by seeding each retired value into a save and reloading: `true`→FULL; `false`/`easy`/`soft`/`off`→DULLED, so anyone who had turned the CRT down is never snapped back up. Touches `frontend/{app/stationui.js,app/world.js,css/style.css,css/app.css,css/marketplace.css}` + the generated `website/app/` mirror; no sidecar, shared, package.json or credential change.

**2026-08-05 merge digest (WALL SIDE FACES + CORNERS — THE MATERIAL REACHES EVERY SURFACE YOU CAN SEE):** `agent/wall-face` → `feat/harness-backend` as merge `b7063ae7` (`--no-ff`) from snapshot `7b004031`; **trunk gate 534/534 green, read from the LOG.** Only the NORTH face ever ran `WALL_RECIPES`. The other three painted one flat `pal.face` fill plus a single rib line, so a room carried its wall HUE all the way round — that part was already right, via a LOCAL SHADOW of the module `wallFace` global that is easy to mistake for a bug — but its MATERIAL stopped at one edge. Symptom: the ten wall materials were near-indistinguishable in a room while their REFIT chips were obviously distinct.

**THE SURFACES DO NOT IMITATE THE RECIPE, THEY SAMPLE IT.** The first cut authored `WALL_EDGES`, a parallel vocabulary meant to RESEMBLE each recipe on the curved and foreshortened faces. Andrew bounced it twice, the second time exactly: *"the textures are completely different ... its literally entirely different set of graphics ... it should literally appear like its the wall, but just continuing on."* He was right and the cause was architectural, not a tuning miss — **an imitation never converges**, because the straight wall is `wallRibbed`'s actual tones and structure while the corner was an approximation of them, and two different pictures meeting at a seam is precisely what you see. The recipe is now rendered ONCE into an offscreen strip and every other surface reads from it: the straight north face draws directly, the tall corner face takes rows 0..len, the foreshortened side takes rows 0..fw. All three are literally the same graphics, differing only in how much of the face's depth is visible and which way the along-axis runs. Transparent samples return null and are skipped so VIEWPORT's glass stays a hole; `viewportRects` is saved and restored so a strip render can never inject phantom windows into the live bake (the guard `sampleWall` already used).

**ONE STRIP PER (MATERIAL, HUE, HEIGHT) — NOT PER TILE.** Anchoring each strip on the tile that asked for it made every wall edge allocate a canvas and a `getImageData`: **51ms → 291ms on an eight-room station, a 5.7× regression**, caught by measuring the lane against trunk in the same page before committing. The tile origin only decides which tile's hash supplies scatter detail (rivets, wear); everything structural is T-periodic and the arc's own anchor is a tile boundary, so a fixed origin stays rib-aligned and costs nothing visible. After: **45.5ms → 63ms, 1.39×**, for painting real material onto three surfaces that previously had none. LAW: **measure a bake change against trunk in the same page** — the `StationBakeBefore` shim plus `performance.now`.

**A CHAMFER HAS TWO FACES AND I FIXED THE SMALL ONE FIRST.** It carries a thin band (the footprint ring bending round) *and*, at a TOP corner only, the region the LIFTED crown ring vacates — which is the north wall's own **tall** face, ~23px deep, coming round the bend, and the one you can actually see. Andrew: *"it should look like the actual WALL on the back wall, it should look like that wall is curving."* Ask which of the two before touching a chamfer.

**ADDRESSING IT TOOK TWO MORE BOUNCES.** Per-slice addressing flipped the along/depth axes at the 45° row/column handoff and the texture stepped there; both are now computed from the pixel's own radius and angle, identical either side. Then arc length — the truer surface coordinate, and the right one for the hull's skirt — turned out to alias here: `a = HR·ang` makes the marks RADIAL so they converge as the radius falls, and at the inner edge RIBBED's 4px pitch lands ~2.5px apart and beats into a checkerboard. **ALONG is now the pixel's own world x, the BACK WALL'S axis**: one unit per pixel at every depth so it cannot beat, and at the north join it IS the straight wall's coordinate, so that seam vanishes rather than narrowing. The cost is the far end of the arc, which foreshortens instead of holding its spacing — that reads as the wall turning away, and Andrew explicitly deprioritised that end (*"focus on blending with the back wall mainly"*). DEPTH stays radial, since that is what carries courses and rails round as concentric bands, and the address is quantized ONCE where it is formed — letting `stripAt` round a second time is its own source of beat.

**THE SOUTH WALL HAS NO VISIBLE INNER FACE.** Andrew: *"we need to remove the wall on the bottom it doesnt make sense to be there due to the angle."* Correct, and a projection error this lane introduced: the camera is above and SOUTH, which is exactly what lets you see the north wall's inner face and by the same geometry forbids the south wall's, since that face points away from you. All you can see of the south wall is its TOP (the crown) and its OUTER face (the hull skirt). The station is now consistently the standard **open box** — north, east and west show inner faces, the wall nearest the camera is cut away — and the sliver inside the tile is a CONTACT SHADOW, not a surface. It had always been a flat dark sliver, so it read as an edge and nobody looked; giving it the material made it assert a face that cannot exist. **LAW: before texturing a surface, ask which way it FACES relative to the camera.**

**2026-08-05 merge digest (BRAND MARK — THE TOPBAR WORDMARK BECOMES THEMED VECTOR ART IN THE GLASS):** `agent/logo-vector-trace` → `feat/harness-backend` as merge `9bd8cf06` from snapshot `b7063ae7`; **trunk gate 534/534 green, read from the LOG**, claims re-locked `204` surface files. Andrew: "it's currently a PNG so it's hard to make it truly look good."

**The mark is now a `<span class="logo-img">` masked by a traced SVG and painted `var(--ph)`** — so it re-tints per theme (the bitmap was gold in amber, green, blue, purple and mono alike) and re-rasterizes at whatever the device asks for (the baked 60px PNG was exact only at DPR 2, soft either side). The trace is **not a redraw** — the distinction that keeps it clear of the reverted `starnet-mark.svg` (661ad745): every coordinate derives from `starnet-logo.png` via `dev/trace-logo.mjs`. The title screen keeps the master PNG, where the ASCII-digit texture has room to read.

**The master art is SPARSE, and that dictates the whole algorithm.** `dev/probe-logo-alpha.mjs`: only ~4.5% of its pixels clear alpha 96, and a mid-height scanline is 2–8px digit strokes separated by 50–200px voids — the letters are hollow outlines drawn out of scattered digits. Thresholding raw alpha yields speckle; the letterform exists only as a **perceived-density field** (area-average the coverage to roughly the size the eye reads it at — the same operation the browser's minification performs — then fuse and threshold). Four rounds, each driven by Andrew looking at a render: (1) traced outline, he picked iso .30 for stroke weight; (2) "rough on the edges" → **smooth the CONTOUR, never the field** — raising sigma flattens the ripple but by 1.8 the four-pointed star in the A has collapsed to a diamond, so a `[1 2 1]` low-pass runs per vertex only where the turn is gentler than 32°, leaving corners, chamfers and the star's points untouched (11 loops before and after — nothing lost — and 10.8 KB → 4.7 KB); (3) "can the CRT filter be applied so it fits in" → **z960 → z935**, under the vignette (940) and scanlines (950) so the beam runs ACROSS the mark instead of stopping at its edges; (4) he chose the **mosaic** preset, the master's own ASCII-dash texture, over the smooth outline.

**Two laws worth carrying.** (a) **The mosaic is SIZE-BOUND and the fix is to COARSEN it, not sharpen it** — at the master's native dash scale it is gorgeous from ~56px and dim mush by 30px, which is the placed-PNG problem returning; averaging the density field down to fh160 merges the dashes into fewer, fatter ones that still resolve at 24–30px. Raising the field height for "more detail" is exactly backwards. (b) **A generated SVG must never emit `--` inside its XML comment** — XML forbids it, the file does not parse, the mask fails, and the masked element renders NOTHING while `getComputedStyle` still reports a perfectly healthy `maskImage`. The generator stamped its own CLI flag into the provenance comment and silently killed the logo; the size-ladder harness was blind to it because inlining markup into HTML uses lenient comment parsing — only the mask path is strict XML. Both are now locked by `test/brand-wordmark-mask.test.js` (registered in fast.list; both faults injected and confirmed to turn it red with a real non-zero exit), along with the viewBox↔`aspect-ratio` pairing and the z-order invariant.

**The hoist is untouched and still does its real job.** `#screen-game` is a z-index:10 stacking context, so ANY z above 10 paints over every floating window — which is why every seat that puts the mark under the glass is still a seat above the windows, and `app/logoclip.js` remains what clips it. Verified live rather than reasoned: with a `.term` parked over the mark it emits a real `path(...)`, none when clear. z960 had existed only because the fixed-amber bitmap was washed muddy by the themed top-glow; themed art dissolved that reason, and the comments asserting it were corrected rather than left lying. `positionLogo()` also gained a device-pixel snap with **one correction pass** (the counter-zoom multiplies the measured-z float error back in, landing ~0.02px off; seat went 55.969 → exactly 56), and the old `img.load` re-seat was deleted — CSS `aspect-ratio` gives a masked span its full width at first layout. Proven across the dial that broke logo seating before: seat holds at 56/56 device px at TEXT SIZE 90/100/115/145 and AUTO, size spread 0.1px (`dev/logo-textsize-proof.mjs`, driven through the real SETTINGS chips — a hand-set `body.zoom` is wiped the moment `applySettings()` re-derives).

**Every visual claim came from a PNG of real device pixels, per the crt-glass lane law.** `dev/logo-live-proof.mjs` clips the actual `#logo` rect out of a CDP screenshot and reports painted coverage, which is the only thing that can prove a mask works: an invalid SVG measured lit fraction **0**, the identical element **0.129** once it parsed. **2026-08-05 merge digest (HULL SKINS — THE STATION EXTERIOR BECOMES A THIRD SURFACE AXIS):** `agent/hull-skins` → `feat/harness-backend` as merge `97480086` (`--no-ff`) from snapshot `375d85e4`; **trunk gate 529/529 green, read from the LOG.** Nine per-room exteriors (station · timber · clapboard · shingle · brick · stone · stucco · curtain · hedge) behind REFIT SURFACE's new `▥ SHELL` target, hue × material like DECK and WALLS, one undo slot per re-clad. The default shell was rebuilt in the same lane, and WHITE joined the palette as bone's achromatic twin.

**The shell was the one surface with no palette at all.** The plate ring, its texture, the framed rim, the corner arcs and the SKIRT — the tall face extruded below the silhouette, which is the surface that actually reads — all came from five hardcoded constants, so every room of every station wore the identical dark riveted hull. Grouping footprints by SKIN is what makes a mixed station read as a street: same-skin neighbours still merge into one unbroken wall (the old whole-station behaviour, preserved), differently-clad ones each get their own, and that boundary is the street. Corridors take their own shell too, so a covered walkway between a cabin and a brick house is a real choice.

**Four laws, each paid for by a wrong first cut.** (1) **Bands are DEPTH, veins are MATERIAL.** The first version emitted one skirt band per course; neighbouring stamps sit at neighbouring points on the same ramp, so a log's shadow and the log above it came out ~0.1 apart and TIMBER and STUCCO rendered as the same flat brown picture. The ramp is six stops and every texture moved to a `source-atop` veins pass. (2) **The hull is the one surface OUTSIDE the ambient mask**, so a `FLOOR_STYLES` hue — chosen to sit dark *after* ambient multiplies it by 0.77 — renders raw out there. Measured down a south wall: station shell 37, TIMBER 51, STONE 55, BRICK 58, and brick's mortar 86, brighter than the lit wall crown at 79. `vacuum()` clamps a hue's luma into the shell band by scaling all three channels by one factor, so the hue survives exactly — an exposure change, the honest model for a surface that gets no light. **But a clamp must not swallow the palette's deliberate poles**: it flattened BONE and WHITE alongside RUST, so picking WHITE handed you another dark grey wall. That is not cohesion, it is the palette lying. Hues already unambiguously bright clamp to their own high ceiling; a white building measures 101 live, above the crown, below the lamps, strictly opt-in. (3) **A course is a CONNECTED contour off each column's wall top.** Ruled in absolute rows it gets SLICED by the corner arc into a ragged staircase; drawn as one flat rect per run it is still a staircase of disconnected dashes. Bridging the step between runs with a one-pixel column is the entire difference. **And never suppress a course to hide an edge artefact** — an earlier "skip runs under 3px" left a bare vertical band exactly where the eye follows the corner, which Andrew circled: the cladding visibly quitting. Fix the connectivity, never the coverage. (4) **A no-geometry fallback must be WORLD-anchored, never canvas row 0** — 69738 px of chunk-parity divergence, latent all lane because `stationbake.chunk.test.js` bakes the DEFAULT shell and the default had no veins until the rebuild. **A parity test only covers the path its fixture exercises.**

**The default shell was the v7 hull verbatim** — a smooth six-stop ramp, one vertical seam, no structure — which is why, beside nine designed materials, the thing everyone starts on read as the empty slot. Now armour STRAKES on an 11px pitch (double BRICK's course: at this scale plate SIZE separates engineering from masonry), a catch-light per plate, a shadow where the plate above overhangs, and rivet rows on the lip — finally keeping the promise the rim always made. Palette untouched, so AUTO is still the shell's own grey. **This deliberately ends the axis's pixel-parity property, on Andrew's explicit call**: until the rebuild, an un-re-clad station baked 0 of 182448 pixels different, verified by diffing a three-room bake against trunk's `stationbake.js` — which is why no golden had to be re-blessed for the axis itself.

**Merge hygiene.** Trunk moved during the lane, so it was merged IN, never rebased; the only conflict was `qa/product-perfect/claims.json`, resolved the lawful way — take one side, complete the merge, REGENERATE off the merge commit (202 locked surface files, `claims.mjs` PASS). Hotfiles `frontend/app/build.js` and `worldmodel.js` both auto-merged and were verified rather than trusted: `node --check` clean, and every hull symbol (`HULL_MATERIALS`, `HULL_ORDER`, `hullMatOfRoom`, `hullStyleOfRoom`, `setHull`, `HULL_RECIPES`, `vacuum`, `skirtTops`, `runsOf`, `courseLine`, `coursedVein`, `sampleHull`, `panelSeam`, `hullSwatchCanvas`) defined exactly once. `package.json` strict-JSON with no BOM; `shared/` untouched; no credential path in the diff. The GHOST PROJECTION lane landed on top mid-gate — all twelve hull commits re-verified as ancestors of the new tip.

**The gate went red twice at DIFFERENT steps and it was the BOX, not the code** (`code-mode` at 526/528, then `shell-machine-state` at 109/529): **0.73 GB free of 15.11 GB, 5%.** That is the documented RAM-starvation signature and the reason the standing law says a different step failing each run means check free RAM. Proven independent of this lane before proceeding: `sidecar/` and `test/code-mode.test.js` are byte-identical between the merge snapshot and HEAD, and the nine suites this lane could plausibly touch (stationbake.hull/chunk/materials, worldmodel, golden, website-app-sync, qa-product-perfect-claims, world-setskin, station-authority) were all green individually. Green on retry once memory freed.

**2026-08-05 merge digest (WORK TRAIL — ONE TOOL CALL, ONE ROW):** `agent/work-trail` → `feat/harness-backend` as merge `76e68479` (`--no-ff`) from snapshot `e3cdde20`; **trunk gate 526/526 green, read from the LOG.** Trunk moved three times during this lane (`4052834e` → `8a5e550e` dialogue read-gate → `e3cdde20` conveyor plan doc), so it was merged in three times, never rebased; the only conflict each round was `qa/product-perfect/claims.json`, resolved the lawful way — take one side, complete the merge, REGENERATE off the merge commit (202 locked surface files, `claims.mjs` PASS). The read-gate round auto-merged `frontend/css/app.css`, verified rather than trusted: braces balance 1788/1788, and a `comm` of trunk's selector set against the merged file shows nothing dropped.

**The double-listing in the work trail was a BUG, not a layout choice.** `endToolRail()` also cleared `pendingChips`, conflating "stop adding chips to that rail" with "forget which calls are still awaiting a result". Order of events for one `fs.write`: the CALL opens a rail and registers its chip → the sidecar's `deliverable` event fires and calls `breakLive()` → `endToolRail()` wipes the map → the tool RESULT arrives, finds nothing pending, and takes `resolveChip`'s ORPHAN path. The Commander was shown the same single call twice, in two different rails: a `pending` chip stuck forever holding the raw arguments, plus a second resolved chip that had lost them. **Proven by probe, not by reading** — call and result share `callId` `call_w1`, yet the DOM held two `.tool-rail`s with one chip each. The map is cleared at run START now, where fresh callIds make a stale pairing impossible.

**The chip head is a label, not a dump.** It printed `brief(argsSummary)` — raw JSON cut at 56 chars — so a write read as a mangled object literal with the filename buried behind punctuation. The salient argument now leads (`fs.write  q3-summary.md`). Critically it **scans rather than parses**: the sidecar caps `argsSummary` at 80 chars on the wire, so the payload is normally a truncated prefix that `JSON.parse` rejects outright — throwing is the common case, not the edge case. The pair regex requires a value's closing quote, so a field the cap cut in half can never be displayed as though it were whole. Related truthfulness fix: the expand implied it held the call's arguments while showing a prefix chopped mid-token, which reads as a malformed call the agent supposedly made; it now says when the record itself is cut.

**Say it once.** The persisted telemetry re-listed every lead call beneath the chips in a third vocabulary (the stored `fs_write` beside the chip's `fs.write`). With chips present the lead block keeps only its header — identity, duration, call count, which the chips genuinely do not carry. Worker blocks always keep their rows, since a dispatched worker's calls never produced chips on this stream.

**Swept before merging, at Andrew's request.** All 27 card scenarios were shot on trunk AND on the lane in the same order and compared: every card identical except the two intended (`21-tool-rail`, `26-run-telemetry`). Two deltas were chased to ground and cleared as artifacts rather than defects — an unanswered `TASK_QUESTION` persisted in the shared seed workspace, which makes every later `nudge()` correctly stand down ("a pending task question owns the moment"), reproduced and confirmed by running those scenarios in isolation; and a once-per-profile `work-rate` coach line already consumed in the lane's browser profile. **The sweep also caught two faults of my own**, both fixed before this merge: (1) removing the `pendingChips` clear from `endToolRail()` left `replayChannel()` with no reset at all — `load()` detaches every chip the map points at, so a snapshot holding a RESULT whose call had been trimmed would have resolved the previous replay's orphaned node invisibly and left the on-screen chip pending forever; (2) a comment of mine claimed the telemetry rows "come back on a reloaded transcript" — they do not, the fold and its telemetry are DOM-only and `hydrateRunTelemetry` runs only at run end on the displayed stream, so neither survives a reload or a stream switch.

**Laws banked:** closing a rail is not the same as orphaning the calls in flight — a pending-call map belongs to the RUN, not the rail, and every path that empties the log owes it a reset. And a wire-capped payload is not JSON: scan it for complete pairs, never assume a parser will take it.

**2026-08-03 merge digest (THE FOREST FLOOR WAS CAMOUFLAGE, AND THE CANOPY WAS LIT FROM THE WRONG SIDE):** `agent/forest-floor` -> `feat/harness-backend` no-ff merge `073b6884` from snapshot `bf26a464` (lane commits `d6ba4b30` sun direction, `2a83283d` floor rewrite, `ac1e6539` ground detail, `52bcc515` website mirror, re-locks `00bc31c5` and `1e6c960b`, plus two trunk syncs `8f0d5f95`/`4f8bd176`). Andrew: the forest "looks really good so far and we're in the right direction, but the grass and dirt and smaller forest details ... almost blend like camouflage when the ground is visible." That was a diagnosis, not a metaphor, and it was exact. **DPM camouflage is ONE recipe** — irregular soft-outlined blobs a few hundred px across, two or three hues at near-equal VALUE, nothing smaller inside them — and the floor was made of that and nothing else: a wetness field at lattice 3 and 7 over a 512 tile drew blobs **170px and 73px wide, i.e. TREE-CROWN SCALE**, choosing between two ramps whose value barely differed, under a dapple of quantized 3-step blobs at 640px. The only other content was 2600 litter flakes / 420 twigs / 700 moss dots drawn **1-3px at 14-50% alpha** — below the size and above the transparency at which an eye resolves a shape, so from any real viewing distance they integrate to a flat wash and contribute nothing. The entire legible content of the surface was therefore two blob fields at the same scale and value as the trees standing on it. **Three moves out, all figure-and-ground:** (1) moss stops being a second ground — one material (duff), moss STIPPLED on with a density fading to zero, so the gather has no outline to read as a patch, and its field runs 4x faster so a gather is always smaller than a crown; (2) the floor gains OBJECTS rather than marks — leaves, needle drift, twigs, grass tufts, surface roots, stones, every one opaque, power-law sized (a few 9px, most 3px) and sitting on its own CONTACT SHADOW, because value structure has to come from objects and value is what the eye segments on; (3) the dapple becomes real SUNFLECKS — the sun's disc through a canopy gap is small, hard-edged, penumbra-ringed and clustered, so small-and-bright reads as a highlight where large-and-mid-value read as paint. **The big noise fields were not thrown away, only moved off the PAINT and onto the POPULATION** — density variation of discrete objects reads as terrain; the identical variation applied to colour is a camo blob. ⛔ **A SHIPPED BUG FOUND ON THE WAY:** `crown()` was lit from the OPPOSITE side to every other object on this ground. `SUN` points from the sun into the scene, so a face is lit when its offset runs ALONG SUN (up-left) — which is how the boulder's lit cap, the log's lit flank and every cast shadow are built — but the crown alone had the term negated, so its leaves were brightest bottom-right **while its own cast shadow fell bottom-right too**. A frame cannot hold two light directions; the eye resolves the contradiction as NO light direction, and that was half of why the ground read as camouflage. Three signs in `crown()` (leaf lighting, shaded well, contact edge) plus the fern frond term, which had the same inversion. Diagnosed by RENDERING one crown at R=150 beside the rock/stump/log, never by reading the sign in the source. Also: ferns were **asterisks** (bare constant-width spines from one point) and are now tapering arced blades with a serrated pinnae comb; boulders were **eggs** (a faceted outline shaded with two concentric discs, which is how you shade a sphere) and are now shaded per FACET so every value boundary is a real edge between two planes; grass tufts were **starbursts** and now leave from a spread of crowns. New pools `tuft` and `deadfall`; undergrowth LOD 0.9x -> 0.55x, since the small end is the wrong thing to cull — culling it leaves only crowns, whose sizes overlap, which is a texture rather than a landscape. Tuning laws earned by looking at renders: **a minority feature spread evenly stops being a feature and becomes the surface** (170 pebbles read as a gravel driveway, 15 roots as a rope network — now 55 and 8); **variable brightness across OVERLAPPING flecks is what makes cotton** (twenty hard discs at twenty amplitudes resolve into a continuous ramp, so amplitude is near-constant and overlaps fuse into one hard pool); **raggedness must scale with the feature** (a 3px fleck given a full-amplitude 4-lobed outline is not ragged, it is a star). Technique: the patch is written straight into the **ImageData buffer**, not through `fillRect` — canvas fills are anti-aliased with no flag to stop it, so a 3px leaf via the 2D API arrives as a grey smudge; bytes give hard pixels, a modulo in the index makes the tile seamless for free with no 3x3 re-stamping, and being able to READ a pixel back is what lets a contact shadow darken what is under it instead of painting a flat patch on top. Whole 512 patch bakes in **~55ms**. Measured offline over the four camera zooms: distinct colour bins (4-bit/channel) **27-52 -> 35-116**, mean luma 0.13-0.15 -> 0.13-0.17, black pixels under 1.3%. **Live-verified on a seeded station @8802 over CDP**, not by screenshot: the FOREST chip clicked in the real SETTINGS window -> `Terrain.getGround()==='forest'`; **magenta sentinel 0%** (a frame not proven repainted is a frame from the previous mode — the REFIT law); **657-783 colour bins** on the real `#stage`; 0 page errors; captures at four zooms. **A shared layer owes a check on every surface that draws it, so THE MOON was switched to and re-proven** — sentinel 0%, 774 bins, no errors. Andrew reviewed the art live and approved. Trunk post-merge `test:fast` **517/517 GREEN, NPM_EXIT=0 and 0 FAIL lines read FROM THE LOG**, claims authority **PASS (37 claims / 193 locked surface files)**; `test:http` **not owed** — the diff is `frontend/app/terrain.js`, its `website/app/` mirror and `claims.json`, no sidecar/route/ship file, no `shared/`, no `package.json`, no credential moved. The tutorial-traps lane landed on trunk mid-gate; its sync conflicted ONLY on `releaseSurface.sourceCommit` and was resolved by taking trunk's ledger whole and **REGENERATING** the surface against the merged tree, never side-picking — the tutorial lane's own digests survive intact, which is the whole reason to regenerate. `frontend/app/build.js` (no-touch hotfile) came in one-sided from that lane and was `node --check`ed and proven byte-identical to trunk. NOT changed, flagged to Andrew rather than silently reworked: **ferns and grass tufts read similarly at world scale** (both small green clumps — distinguishing them further is a sprite lane, not a floor fix), and **stumps are now the plainest prop out there** relative to the detail the ground gained around them. **2026-08-03 merge digest (THE CONTEXT GAUGE WAS READING A DIFFERENT CHAT):** `agent/ctxwin` -> `feat/harness-backend` no-ff merge `422136bf` from snapshot `cdd04226` (lane commits `f1148003` per-conversation keying, `6be3a2c2` baseline projection, `67edb810` trunk sync, in-lane re-locks `c7a73f39`/`2c071ab5`/`d72d7cc0`; `169aed66` re-lock AGAIN at the merge commit, since a mid-merge regeneration records the wrong sourceCommit). Andrew: the context window is "still very inaccurate ... can't properly showcase the context window with the bar." Reproduced live on a seeded station against real OpenRouter turns, and the numerator was never the problem — the KEY was. Occupancy lived in `contextByAgent[agentId]`, while the bottom bar labels itself "MEMORY OF THIS CHAT": a workstream with **ZERO turns read `13k / 200k` (7% full)**, inherited from a 4-turn sibling, and after a long session that is an empty chat claiming most of the window. It also only moved on a completed model call, so a session resumed from disk sat on `—` until you paid for another turn — most of what "it never works" actually felt like. Readings now key on **(agentId, streamId)**; `chat()` binds each runId to the workstream that launched it at `agent.run.start` (run.start always precedes agent.cost on that stream), and a server-launched cron/channel run with no registered conversation folds to a streamless bucket — real occupancy that must never repaint the open chat. To make a chat readable BEFORE it has been measured, the harness overhead (system prompt + tool schemas + sidecar dressing — **measured ~13.2k tokens against a two-line chat**, so a browser char/4 estimate alone is an order of magnitude short and worse than useless) is learned as `prompt_tokens − our own estimate of the messages we sent`, from the **FIRST cost event of a run only**: later turns of an agentic run carry accumulated tool results the next request never resends, and calibrating on a turn-4 61k prompt inflated it ~4x. ⛔ The live walk then caught a defect in the fix itself: a measurement can land BELOW the transcript we handed over, and that is **`context.js` compacting at 0.65 of the window**, NOT a tokenizer disagreeing. Fitting a per-model shrink factor to that gap (the first attempt) painted **~120k against a real ~30k prompt** and would have understated every other chat on that model — compaction is a fact about ONE conversation. Corrected: `calibrate()` returns null there (learn nothing about the model, keep the last good fit) and that conversation grows from **its own baseline** — the real reading of that exact transcript plus only what has been said since, which already contains its true overhead and whatever was folded away. Derived numbers are marked `projected`, rendered with a leading `~` and stamped `data-provenance` so nothing can mistake them for a measurement; the fit is persisted to `starnet.ctx.overhead` (validated on read, dropped if not a usable fit) because an un-persisted calibration blanks the gauge on every reload. Bar: ten whole cells over a 200k window is one notch per 20k, so 5% and 14% painted identically — new `AsciiFX.barCells` floors the lit cells and reports a **half cell** (same glyph dimmed via `.ctx-half`) for 20 steps in the same width, keeping AsciiFX's two honesty rules and introducing no glyph that could fall out of VT323 and change a cell's advance mid-bar. Verified live on seeded station @9455 with real turns: **real prompt 13,270 vs the gauge's 13,275** (5 tokens); a brand-new session reads the harness floor `~13k` instead of inheriting the sibling; switching between a long and a short chat tracks the conversation on screen (~58% / ~7%, both directions, DOM-confirmed with a full ctxTick between switches); calibration survives a reload. New `test/ctx-conversation-scope.test.js` runs the REAL registerRun/foldContextCost/endContextRun/contextState bodies sliced out of harness.js in a vm sandbox and replays run-in-A-then-read-B (reverting to per-agent keying fails it on a VALUE, not a missing symbol); `ctx-model-catalog.test.js`'s slice anchor accepts both the old and new occupancy comment so it stays red against `1fa14b35^1` as verified. Trunk post-merge `test:fast` **511/511 GREEN, EXIT=0, 0 FAIL lines read from the log**, claims authority PASS; `test:http` not owed (frontend/test/website only). Two unrelated timing reapers flaked across gate runs (`agent-eval`, `lsp-edit-feedback`) — different assertion sets per run, both green alone and on re-run, neither touched by this lane. Grepping the GATE rather than the symptom shows `makeDriver` returns the inert driver unless `deps.allowPhysicalInput === true` and `win32DriverActive()` hard-returns `false`, and `index.js` registers it with `allowPhysicalInput: false` as deliberate defence in depth. So it was a CONTRACT defect on a path that never runs; the capability hole that actually bit was `fs.read`, which could not show the agent an image on disk — including `image_generate`'s own output. **LAW: grep the gate before ranking a gap by its symptom.**
- **⛔ LAW — A CHANNEL WITH ONE PRODUCER IS A SPECIAL CASE, NOT A CHANNEL.** The 07-27 pixel fix was wired at a single call site (`browser.js`), which is exactly why the 07-28 audit found the same gap again at two more producers. The fix is one shared DECISION MODULE — `imagewire.sniff/toWire` is the only place that answers "may these bytes go on the wire", so both producers answer identically and a third gets it free. Sniffing is by **magic bytes, never extension**: a mislabelled `.png` falls THROUGH to the plain read. An unsupported mime (BMP/TIFF/ICO) sniffs so the tool can say "convert it" but is a **400, never a graceful degrade** — only png/jpeg/gif/webp are accepted by every vision provider.
- **⛔ STDIN TO A BACKGROUND PROCESS IS A SCREEN BYPASS UNLESS YOU SCREEN IT.** A line typed into a `bash`/`python` REPL executes exactly like a `shell.exec` command, so `shell.bg.write` runs the same `commandSafetyRisk` guard and is consent-gated — its sibling bg tools are not, and that asymmetry is deliberate.
- **A RING BUFFER MUST CUT ON A LINE BOUNDARY.** The ring grew 16KB->256KB and now reports `truncatedStart`/`droppedBytes`: once it laps, line 1 is NOT the first line printed, and an agent that assumes otherwise locates a failure in the wrong place. A mid-line cut hands back a fragment that reads like a real line and nothing downstream can tell.
- **WATER-FILL, DON'T SCALE PROPORTIONALLY.** `loop.js applyTurnBudget` caps the aggregate tool output of one TURN (200k default) — N parallel tools at 80k each blew the window even with per-tool parking in place. A proportional cut shaves the 900-char result to make room for the 300k one, and the short result is usually the answer.
- **QUOTA BUCKETS MERGE, NEVER REPLACE — AND EMPTY IS NO DATA, NEVER HEADROOM.** `providers/ratelimits.js` learns quota from the `*-remaining` headers of ordinary SUCCESSFUL calls instead of only from a 429, wired at the factory's `opts.fetch` seam so all five adapters are instrumented in one edit (a sixth adapter gets it free; five separate edits is the one a sixth never remembers). A cached call can omit token counters, so wholesale replacement would make a bucket vanish from the readout **as though the limit had been lifted**. `/api/diagnostics` prints "not observed yet" in words rather than a blank section that reads as an all-clear.
- **⛔ THE MERGE COLLIDED WITH ANOTHER SESSION'S UNCOMMITTED WORK IN THE INTEGRATION TREE, AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT WAS REFUSED.** A live session had `sidecar/index.js` + `sidecar/mcp/manager.js` modified and three new untracked files (an agent-lifecycle module) — none of it committed. **2026-07-28 digest (AGENTIC BROWSING — conditional waits, stale-ref recovery, the Commander's own Chrome, and finding past the cap):** `1536a278` + `0fb137b2`, **committed DIRECTLY to `feat/harness-backend`, NOT through a lane merge** — see the process note at the end, which is the most important line here. Gate **test:fast 430 green ON TRUNK** (re-run in an isolated worktree AFTER the three lanes that merged on top: learned-topic recommendations, COMMS composer fit, and the folder-card consent fix), claims planning authority **PASS**. Diff is `sidecar/tools/builtin/browser.js`, `sidecar/capability/registry.js` and four test files — **no frontend, no `shared/`, no `package.json`, nothing in the release surface, so NO claims re-lock is owed** (checked against `releaseSurface.files`, not assumed). 71 new assertions across `test/browser.wait-recovery.test.js` and `test/browser.attach.test.js`; both revert-checked (disable recovery, or delete the eval refusal, and they go red).
- **⛔ LAW — COUNT TOOLS BY LOADING THE MODULE, NEVER BY GREPPING `name:`.** The browser surface was reported as 35, then 52, then **79** tools across three consecutive turns, and every undercount had one cause: these tools are declared through helpers — `read('browser.click', …)`, `exec(…)` — where **the name is the first POSITIONAL ARGUMENT**, not a `name:` property. A `name:` grep silently drops whole families (all 29 `browser.*`, plus `web_*`, `image_*`, `voice_generate`, `spotify_*`). The honest count is `require()` the module and read `.tools.map(t => t.name)`.
- **LAW — AUDIT THE SUBSYSTEM BEFORE RATING IT.** On the strength of that grep this browser was scored a gap that "drives pixels via computer.use and a vision sub-call". It does not, and never did: `browser.js` is ~1900 lines of real CDP driver with ref-based accessibility snapshots, out-of-process iframe adoption, popup auto-attach, downloads already routed into the agent's jail, and `browser.login` banking real signed-in sessions behind a single-owner profile lease. It also already made a call Hermes does not: **`eval` refused ON the signed-in profile**, because "eval is dangerous WHERE THE CREDENTIALS ARE". A rating sourced from a grep is a guess wearing a number.
- **LAW — A TIMEOUT IS A FINDING, NOT A FAILURE.** `browser.wait` never throws on timeout and never reads as success — "the results never loaded" is a real answer the agent has to be able to branch on. A THROWN predicate (bad selector) is reported immediately as a malformed question instead of burning the budget and then reporting absence: different diagnosis, different next move. And it waits on **visibility, not presence** — `display:none`, a zero-size box and a collapsed parent all match `querySelector`, so waiting on presence is how an agent walks into a still-hidden dialog.
- **LAW — `navEpoch` IS NOT `version`, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE SAFETY ARGUMENT.** `version` bumps on snapshot AND on navigation, so it cannot tell them apart — and that is exactly what decides whether a stale ref may be recovered. Re-snapshotting only renumbers the same page; a navigation or tab switch replaces the document, where the same role+text is a DIFFERENT control. `back`/`forward`/`tab_select` bump the epoch too.
- **LAW — RECOVERY USES FRESH COORDINATES, WHICH IS WHY IT RETIRES THE OLD CONTRACT RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT.** Two existing tests asserted a stale ref must REJECT, guarding against a "silently mis-aimed" click. Recovery re-snapshots and takes the new node, so it never touches the remembered coordinates — the guarded hazard is eliminated, not tolerated. Ambiguity still fails loudly (two matching "Delete" buttons name the candidates rather than flip a coin on a mutating action), and recovery is never silent.
- **LAW — ONE RE-SNAPSHOT RESOLVES EVERY REF IN A CALL.** Recovering refs one at a time re-snapshots per ref, and each pass invalidates the ref the previous pass just resolved — so a two-ref `browser.drag` could never have recovered at all. Found by reading my own diff before the gate, not by a test.
- **ATTACH — THE HONEST ANSWER TO BOT WALLS.** Hermes' extra engines are lightpanda and **Camoufox** (a Firefox fork with C++ fingerprint spoofing, ~300MB plus its own REST server). No stealth was built here and nothing is lost by that: `browser.attach` drives the Commander's OWN running Chrome over its DevTools port — a real browser, a real profile, their real sessions, no download and no deception. Its guards: consent ALWAYS (never defaulted away), **`eval` stays refused for as long as the session is attached** (their browser holds every login they have, not just the ones they chose to lend the station), the attachment is **sticky** so a headless request cannot silently swap in a station browser mid-task, the port is probed BEFORE the relaunch so a wrong port does not cost a working session, the probe is **127.0.0.1-only** (a DevTools port is unauthenticated RCE over the browser), and `proc` stays null so `close()` — which only kills what it spawned — can never shut their browser and its unsaved tabs.
- **LAW — A ZERO-HIT ANSWER MUST SAY WHICH KIND OF ZERO IT IS.** `browser.find` scans at the driver's 200 ceiling instead of snapshot's 80, and reports `scanned`/`capped`, because "not on this page" and "past the cap" are different next moves and the agent cannot guess between them.
- **THE REPO'S OWN GUARDS CAUGHT THE ONE DEFECT THAT MATTERED.** `browser.tool-parity.test` found `browser.wait` **registered but NOT GRANTED** in `CAP_REGISTRY` — it would have shipped invisible to every real agent. **A new tool needs BOTH a registration and a grant**, plus the locked surface lists in `test/browser.test.js` and `test/harness.integration.test.js`. Deferral was chosen per tool for a measured reason: `wait`/`find` are front-row (a waiting tool the model cannot see is one it replaces with a guess), `attach`/`detach` are deferred (the browser family is already ~10.2KB of schema on every turn).
- **NOT BUILT, ON PURPOSE.** `browser.cookies` — reading cookies is a credential-exfiltration primitive that would have to be refused in exactly the signed-in cases where it would be useful; `browser.inspect`/`get_text` cover the honest uses. Downloads were **checked and found already solved** (Chrome is pointed at the agent's jailed `downloads/`), so no duplicate was built. Still open: `browser.pdf`, `browser.intercept`, `browser.emulate`.

- **RAW MARKDOWN REACHED THE PHONE — visible in the member's own screenshots.** Every reply left the sidecar as plain text with NO `parse_mode`, so an LLM's ordinary output arrived as literal `**bold**`, backticks, `## headings`, ``` fences. `channels/telegram.format.js` converts only the subset it can PROVE is balanced and the transport sends `parse_mode:'HTML'`. **The fallback is the point:** a malformed entity string is a 400 and the message is LOST, so a parse rejection resends ONCE unformatted and marker-stripped — the floor is exactly the old behaviour minus the noise. Only entity errors retry; a 403 would fail identically twice. `_underscore_` and lone `*` are NEVER emphasis (snake_case tool names and bullets are commoner here than the emphasis they would imply), and an unpaired marker left by a chunk split stays literal rather than emitting an unclosed tag. `editMessageText` got the same treatment or a consent card delivered formatted would be rewritten into raw syntax the instant its button was tapped. **`WEB & BROWSER` in the /tools card is the cautionary case: an unescaped `&` is exactly what would have 400'd an HTML send.**
- **"/start" SPENT A PAID MODEL RUN.** Telegram shows a START button on every fresh chat and sends that literal text when pressed — the first thing a new member ever transmits. It was in no command table, fell through `parseCommand` as an ordinary message, and the member's first exchange with the station was an agent puzzling over the word "/start". Answered by the hub now, free. Unknown commands still fall through to a run unchanged — that is a TESTED decision (a path like `/usr/bin/x` must still reach the agent), so only `/start` was added.
- **AN UNPARSEABLE UPDATE COULD WEDGE THE WHOLE CHANNEL.** `dispatch()` swallowed a `normalize()` throw and returned WITHOUT advancing the offset; getUpdates keeps returning everything at-or-after `offset` until a higher one confirms it, so the loop would re-fetch and re-throw on that same update forever — a hot spin against the Bot API with every message behind it permanently undelivered. It now advances from the raw `update_id`.
- **TRAP FOR THE NEXT LANE: a new test file is NOT in the gate until it is in `test/fast.list`.** `scripts/run-fast-tests.mjs` reads an explicit list, not a glob. The first full gate here reported **exit 0 with the new test never executed** — green having verified nothing. Grep the gate log for the test's own OK line before believing it ran.
- **The integration tree was occupied by another live session** (uncommitted `browser.wait` work in `registry.js`/`browser.js` + a `harness.integration.test` expectation mid-update). That turned a full gate in-tree red on a tool this lane never touched, so the gate was re-run in a clean worktree instead, and only this lane's files were staged. `test/fast.list` carried BOTH sessions' additions: theirs was stripped for the commit (trunk must never reference an uncommitted test file) and restored to their working tree afterwards.

New `sidecar/skills/gate.js` is the consumer. **LAW — when auditing a security surface, grep the CONSUMER, not the producer**; a stamped verdict nobody reads is a comment. Same family as [[injected-dependency-hides-wiring-bugs]].
- **⛔ SECOND DEAD FEATURE, FOUND ONLY BY LOOKING AT THE PROVIDER'S BYTES: `/skill` PRELOAD HAD NEVER WORKED.** `sidecar/index.js` read the bare identifier `preloadSkills` inside `runOnce` — that is `handleRun`'s local — so the line threw ReferenceError on EVERY run and its own `catch` ("explicit skill preload must never break a run") swallowed it without a word. `/skill Name` loaded nothing; `body.preloadSkills` was ignored. **LAW — a catch whose comment says "must never break a run" will hide a dead feature forever.** Units and a booted-host HTTP test both passed while it was dead.
- **LAW — ONLY ASSERTING ON THE BYTES THAT REACH THE PROVIDER CAN SEE A SKIPPED PROMPT BLOCK.** `test/skills.gate.prompt.e2e.test.js` boots the real sidecar against a mock upstream (`SKYNET_OPENROUTER_BASE`) and asserts on the composed system prompt: the withheld skill is NAMED but carries no summary and no body, the flagged text appears NOWHERE in the request, a withheld `/skill` is stated out loud, a clean one preloads with its real steps, and after approval the body IS delivered. Two traps in that rig: **one `/api/run` POST produces MORE than one upstream call** (aux self-talk/session titling lands in the same capture, so `requests[last]` reads the TITLING call and finds no index — take the window and pick the run by its `[RUNTIME]` marker), and **a mock model must advertise `supported_parameters:['tools']`** or an `isTask` run is refused before composing anything and nothing reaches the mock at all.
- **A WITHHELD SKILL IS NAMED, NEVER SUMMARIZED.** Hiding the row makes the model create a same-named skill, which `manage()` then refuses as a duplicate — a silent gate that manufactures a confusing refusal two turns later. The summary is dropped because it is model-authored text the scan never covered.
- **`hydrate()` OVERRIDES THE STORED BODY FROM DISK**, so the bytes `skill.view` delivers are not necessarily the bytes `persist()` scanned — an edited `SKILL.md` laundered content past the scanner. The gate re-digests at the delivery seam and re-scans live on a mismatch, taking the worse action; legacy records (written before the guard existed, carrying no verdict at all) are live-scanned there too.
- **`block` IS NOT APPROVABLE, `ask` IS — AND THE COMMANDER'S OWN TYPING GETS ITS OWN TIER.** Scanning human-authored content as `trusted` (dangerous -> block) made a dead end the moment verdicts were enforced: you write `rm -rf` into your own procedure deliberately and the only surface that could bless it is the one refusing you. `guard.js` gains a `user` tier that ASKS; `trusted`/`community` keep block, which is the right answer for content that ARRIVES claiming someone else vetted it. **An approval blesses BYTES, not a name** (the `plugins-allowed.json` law) — keyed to a content digest, proven to survive a sidecar restart and to re-ask after an edit.

- **TRUNK MOVED UNDER THE GATE — THE RED I SAW WAS NOT MINE.** The connectors/voice lane merged (`53e01dd5`) while my post-merge `npm test` was running and changed `frontend/app/toolprops.js`, a locked surface file, so `qa-product-perfect-claims` went BLOCKED at step 170/424.
