Clean ort merge, zero conflicts; `sidecar/index.js` auto-merged, so it was `node --check`ed and `composeOffice`/`defaultObjects`/`officeSurface` were each grepped to exactly one definition afterwards. **Lands AFTER the `v0.7.0` tag (`799b8b06`) — it does NOT ride that cut unless the tag moves.** Reported by a member off the **v0.7.0** install that shipped the `/tools` readout fix: "/tools work and they don't".

- **THE BUG: A CONSENT OPT-IN SILENTLY COST THE AGENT ITS OFFICE.** The hub runs `surface: wantApprovals ? 'interactive' : 'autonomous'`, and `runOnce` fed that same word to `composeOffice`. `surface` was carrying **two orthogonal meanings** — *who answers an ungranted mutation* and *whether this run has a real floor to read placed props off*. `'interactive'` means THE MOAT: the office starts COMPUTE-ONLY and a browser appends the agent's actually-placed props via `extraObjects`. A phone never sends `extraObjects` and has no floor at all, so `/approvals on` dropped the chat to the wire's `brief_ask brief_proceed tool_search quest_update` — 4 tools, no web, no files, no notebook — the moment the Commander asked to be consulted.
- **BOTH HALVES OF THE MEMBER'S SCREENSHOTS WERE HONEST.** `/tools` (fixed the day before, `71806559`) correctly described the autonomous office; the agent correctly reported it had no web. The tell was the agent quoting StarNet's *"Every tool you have been granted is already listed"* — that string is `sidecar/tools/builtin/toolsearch.js:114` and is reachable ONLY on an EMPTY deferred set, while the autonomous office defers 16 browser tools. Approvals-ON is the only state that produces it: a non-task turn advertises no tools at all (so `tool.search` would not exist to be quoted), and approvals-OFF would have handed back 16 deferrals.
- **THE FIX.** `floorless: true` on the hub's `runOnce` call; `officeSurface = o.floorless ? 'autonomous' : surface`. The consent and taint semantics of `'interactive'` are deliberately untouched — a human IS answering over the inline keyboard. The moat still holds where it is genuinely a floor fact: no `shell_exec`, no `team_dispatch`, however approvals are set.
- **PROOF AT THE WIRE, NOT AT A READOUT** (a readout is what lied here in the first place): `channels.telegram.e2e` drives `/approvals on` through the real Telegram ingress and asserts the tool list that reaches the PROVIDER. Reverting `floorless` turns it red on exactly the member's symptom. Note the wire spells a dotted tool with an underscore (`fs.read` -> `fs_read`) — registry-spelled assertions would pass vacuously forever.
- **WORKAROUND for anyone on v0.7.0 today: `/approvals off`** restores the full office immediately; `/status` reports the flag.

**2026-07-28 merge digest (the agent voice died after its first few words — one TTS blip guillotined the rest of the reply):** `claude/voice-mode-sound-bug-0b3d7b` -> `feat/harness-backend` no-ff merge `10f98c56` (snapshot/reset point `3e3298d0`; the lane carries its own claims re-lock `d75dd0f8`). Gate **ON TRUNK after the merge: test:fast 423 green, claims planning PASS (37 claims / 184 locked paths)**; `test:http` ran green on the branch content and is **not owed** — the diff touches no sidecar/route/ship file. 4 files, +165/-39 — `frontend/app/voice.js`, its generated `website/app/` mirror, `test/voice.button.test.js`, `claims.json`. **No hotfile from the no-touch set, no `shared/`, no `package.json`, no credential moved.** Clean ort merge, zero conflicts. **Lands AFTER the `v0.7.0` tag (`799b8b06`) — like the CTX gauge and Telegram `/tools` fixes, it does NOT ride that cut unless the tag moves.** Reported by a member off a **v0.6.8** install: with the agent voice on, the agent speaks its opening words and then goes dead quiet for the whole rest of the reply.

- **THE BUG: A FAILED CHUNK'S COLD-OFF SILENCED EVERY LATER CHUNK OF THE SAME REPLY.** A spoken reply is streamed to `/api/tts` sentence-by-sentence, and `chat.js:5843` deliberately flushes the FIRST chunk after ~3-4 words so audio starts fast. In `startSynth` (`frontend/app/voice.js`) any failed chunk armed a 4s `neuralColdUntil`, and every later chunk of the SAME reply then short-circuited straight to `{kind:'silent'}` **without even attempting its round-trip**. So one transient 429/network blip on sentence 2 killed sentences 3..N, and all the member heard was that first flushed chunk — which is exactly "it only says the first word".
- **LAW — A BACKOFF MUST NEVER GUILLOTINE WORK ALREADY IN FLIGHT.** Gate new work on a cold-off, never the remainder of a stream that has already started producing. The symptom of getting this wrong is always "it starts, then stops dead", and it reads to the user as a total feature failure rather than the one-chunk blip it actually is. The fix lets a reply that has already ATTEMPTED a synth outrank the cold-off until it has failed `MID_REPLY_GIVEUP` (2) times in a row; a brand-new reply still honors it in full, so a genuinely dead provider is still not hammered once per sentence.
- **LAW — A SUCCESS MUST LIFT THE COLD-OFF.** `noteNeuralOk` cleared the failure counters but not `neuralColdUntil`, so a blip kept suppressing calls the path had *just proven* it could serve — including the next reply's opening words.
- **PROVEN LIVE ON A SEEDED DEV STATION, BOTH DIRECTIONS, NOT ARGUED FROM THE SOURCE.** Rig worth reusing for any voice-output bug: boot a seed, patch `HTMLMediaElement.prototype.play` + `window.fetch` to log, force a 429 on the Nth `/api/tts`, drive five `Voice.speakChunk()` then `endReply()`, count `play()` calls. **Before: 1 of 5 chunks played. After: 4 of 5** (the one lost chunk is the one whose original AND retry were both forced to fail), and **5 of 5** when the blip is a true one-shot.
- **TRAP — A RETRY CAN MASK THE FIX YOU ARE TESTING.** The first regression test failed exactly one request; the new one-shot retry rescued it and the test stayed **green with the cold-off fix reverted**. A blip must outlive the retry (fail request N *and* N+1) for the cold-off gate to be exercised at all. Both halves are now proven by reverting each independently and watching them go red — 4 assertions for the gate, 1 for the retry.
- Also fixed: one immediate retry for a **transient** class only (429/network/5xx — `no key`/billing are never retried, they are not transient), and the speaker-on `prewarmVoice()` — ~6 background synth calls for the persona's stock lines — now **yields while `draining`** instead of racing the live reply's chunks against the same provider. That concurrency is the most likely way the member's "turn voice on, then turn sound on" sequence produced the 429 in the first place; the amplifier that turned it into a dead reply is what was proven and fixed.
- **THE CLAIMS RE-LOCK WAS OWED AND THE FIRST MERGE WAS RESET FOR IT.** `frontend/app/voice.js` is one of the 184 locked release-surface files, so the fix moved its bytes and `qa-product-perfect-claims` went BLOCKED at step 169/423 **on trunk**. Attribution was measured, not assumed — the test was run in clean detached worktrees at both the pre-merge snapshot (**green**) and the merged HEAD (**red**), which is what proved it was the merge and not the main tree's uncommitted `qa/STATUS.md` drift. Trunk was `reset --hard` to `3e3298d0` per the ritual, the re-lock was done **on the branch** as its own commit (path set IDENTICAL, `pathSetSha256` unchanged, exactly one hash moved, `sourceCommit` `db0dbc81` -> `12910b7b`), and the branch was re-gated green before re-merging. **Never fix a claims BLOCK forward on trunk — the re-lock belongs to the lane.**
- **GUARDIAN IS RED AT THIS COMMIT WITH THE SAME TWO P1s, BOTH PRE-EXISTING AND NEITHER TOUCHED BY THIS LANE:** `J1.2-run-live::crew/working-covers-busy` (the racy sample point already triaged at the v0.7.0 cut) and `log/frozen-bus` (stamped at `7af7a1de`, v0.6.8's own commit). Verified present on trunk *before* this merge; this digest does not re-assert them as new.

**2026-07-28 merge digest (Telegram `/tools` reported an empty toolset the agent DID have):** `claude/telegram-tools-missing-e879ae` -> `feat/harness-backend` no-ff merge `71806559` (snapshot/reset point `11a7ced6`). Gate **ON TRUNK after the merge: test:fast 423 green + full test:http, both exit 0**. 2 files, +41/-3 — `sidecar/index.js`, `test/channels.telegram.e2e.test.js`. **No hotfile from the no-touch set, no `shared/`, no `package.json`, no credential moved, no claims needle touched** (the user-facing copy is unchanged — only which branch of it is reached), so no W0 re-stamp owed. Clean ort merge, zero conflicts. **Lands AFTER the `v0.7.0` tag (`799b8b06`) — like the CTX gauge fix, it does NOT ride that cut unless the tag moves.**

Reported by a member off a **v0.6.8** install: Telegram was connected and identified itself correctly, but `/tools` answered *"This agent has no tools yet — place props in REFIT"* with EVERY family listed as locked, while the same agent had working web/files/terminal/memory on the desktop. They had already disconnected/reconnected Telegram and restarted the session, and were about to re-issue the bot token.

- **THE BUG WAS THE READOUT, NOT THE GRANT — THE TOOLS HAD BEEN THERE THE WHOLE TIME.** `runSlashForChannel` (`sidecar/index.js`) derived `placed` **only** from `router.stationFor(agentId)`. That function is **BAY-ONLY**: it returns `null` for any agent not docked in a conveyor bay — i.e. essentially every main agent — and the caller read that `null` as an empty room, so `placed=[]` and every family fell into "locked until placed". Meanwhile the agent's Telegram **runs** were unaffected: `hub.js:985` passes `station: undefined`, `runOnce` then composes `composeOffice({surface:'autonomous'})` = computer/dish/cabinet/notebook/studio/jukebox. The command lied about a capability set that was working. **Nothing the member did could have helped, and re-issuing the bot token would have changed nothing.**
- **LAW — `stationFor()` RETURNING `null` MEANS "NOT IN A BAY", NEVER "NO TOOLS".** Every caller needs an explicit non-bay branch. This is the whole bug in one sentence, and the same misread is available to any future caller of that function.
- **LAW — A CAPABILITY READOUT MUST BE COMPUTED FROM THE SAME EXPRESSION THE RUN RESOLVES AGAINST.** The two halves were each locally correct and disagreed only in composition, which is why nothing looked wrong on inspection: the fix derives `placed` from the SAME two sources the channel's runs use — the bay if `stationFor` is non-null, else `composeOffice({surface:'autonomous', lead:false})`.
- **LAW — A HEADLESS SURFACE IS NOT THE DESKTOP FLOOR; DO NOT QUOTE `heroCaps` THERE.** Deliberately NOT fixed by reporting the desktop's placed props, which would trade one lie for another: by design (`sidecar/capability/office.js`) Telegram/cron/delegated runs keep the default office, so a placed **WORKBENCH grants no terminal over Telegram** and **TASK DELEGATION is LEAD-only**. The corrected `/tools` lists web/files/memory/studio/jukebox as active and still shows those two as locked — which is the truth for that surface. The member should be told this explicitly; it is the one part of their expectation the fix does not satisfy.
- **PROVEN BY REVERTING THE FIX, NOT BY WATCHING IT PASS.** The guard lives in `channels.telegram.e2e` and drives real Telegram ingress (mock Bot API -> `getUpdates` -> hub -> `runSlash`), with **no routing plan posted — so `stationFor` is null exactly as on a real station**, which is what makes it a true reproduction rather than a mocked one. With the fix reverted it goes red on the member's exact sentence (`FAIL: /tools over Telegram does NOT claim the agent has no tools`). It also pins the negative half (no WORKBENCH / TASK DELEGATION in the `✓` lines) and that a slash command spends **no model turn**.
- **BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER THAN TELEGRAM, IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION.** `runSlashForChannel` is shared by Discord, the DEV channel, and `runSlashRoutine` (a scheduled `/`-prompt), so all of them were reporting the same empty toolset and all are fixed at once. It also feeds `slashOptions(placed)` -> the skills catalog, so skills `requires:`-gated on dish/cabinet/notebook now correctly resolve off-browser — matching the caps those runs genuinely hold. The run-time capability gate (`resolveTools`) is untouched, so this widens no actual grant.

**2026-07-28 the manual installer could not overwrite its own node.exe — FIXED on the v0.7.0 cut surface (`799b8b06`):** Andrew ran the candidate installer and got **"Error opening file for writing: …\AppData\Local\StarNet\node.exe"** with Abort/Retry/Ignore. Diagnosed to the end rather than worked around: Tauri's `CheckIfAppIsRunning` (utils.nsh) only ever kills `${MAINBINARYNAME}.exe` — the shell — and does it with a hard `TerminateProcess`, which runs NEITHER `Drop for AppState` NOR the `ExitRequested` handler where `kill_sidecar()` lives. So it **strands** the sidecar, and the very next thing the Install section does is `File` over `node.exe`. Interactively that stops on the dialog; **silently (`/S`) it is WORSE — the error is auto-ignored and the install completes carrying a STALE node.exe** (measured: mtime unchanged, locker still alive, installer exit 0). Fixed with `src-tauri/installer/hooks.nsh`, an `NSIS_HOOK_PREINSTALL` that kills the shell and then the sidecar, matched on FULL IMAGE PATH, before the file copy. Gate ON TRUNK after: **test:fast 423 + full test:http, exit 0**, claims planning PASS.
- **THE IN-APP UPDATER PATH WAS ALREADY SAFE — CHECK BEFORE YOU PANIC, AND CHECK BEFORE YOU HEDGE.** `main.rs:1836` already carries an `on_before_exit` hook that calls `kill_sidecar()` before the updater plugin's `std::process::exit`, added and canary-proven 2026-07-14 and shipped in v0.6.7 and v0.6.8. Its comment describes Andrew's dialog word for word. UPDATE CENTER users were never affected. The gap was only the MANUAL download path and the ORPHAN path (a sidecar stranded by an earlier hard kill, whose parent is long gone — the Rust reaper only runs at the NEXT app boot, i.e. after the installer has already failed). Andrew's case was both at once: an orphan from ~21h earlier, parent already dead.
- **LAW — ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: THE SHELL DIES FIRST.** A guardian thread polls the child every ~3s and respawns it on unexpected exit (`spawn_guardian`), gated only by an in-process `shutting_down` flag a hard kill never sets. Kill `node.exe` while the shell is alive and it is back, holding the same lock, within three seconds.
- **LAW — SCOPE IS LOAD-BEARING: KILL BY FULL IMAGE PATH, NEVER BY NAME.** Tauri's own `KillProcess` matches by executable NAME. On this machine that would have killed **18 unrelated `node.exe` processes** — other apps, dev servers, other agent runtimes. Same rule `main.rs` already states for its own reaper: "Full image path — the ONLY thing that authorizes a kill."
- **LAW — THE NSIS INSTALLER IS A 32-BIT PROCESS, SO `$SYSDIR` IS WOW64-REDIRECTED.** The first version of the hook did nothing at all and reported success: `$SYSDIR\WindowsPowerShell` resolves to SysWOW64, and a 32-bit PowerShell can SEE 64-bit processes but reads their `.Path` as **EMPTY** — so the path-scoped match found nothing and exited 0. Measured directly: `Get-Process -Id <64-bit pid> | Select Path` returns the real path under System32 PowerShell and blank under SysWOW64. Reaching the 64-bit PowerShell via the `SysNative` alias is the fix. **It failed SAFE (killed nothing) rather than dangerous — a name-based kill would have failed CATASTROPHICALLY in the same spot.**
- **LAW — INSTRUMENT, DO NOT THEORIZE.** Four wrong hypotheses were burned on why the hook was a no-op (NSIS `$\'` escaping, plugin availability, silent-mode skipping, guardian respawn). What settled it in one shot was a temporary debug build whose hook wrote `$INSTDIR`, `$SYSDIR`, the exit code and the captured stdout to a file: `hook ran / probe_rc=0 / probe_out=[]` said unambiguously that the command ran and matched nothing.
- **LAW — A CORRELATION FROM ONE SAMPLE IS NOT A CAUSE.** The first scoped test showed "2 unrelated node processes killed", and a 30s no-op control showed 0 — which looked damning. Nine INTERLEAVED trials (hook-commands / no-op-spawn / sleep-only) then showed **0 unrelated deaths in every arm**, and the node population had decayed 23→16 on its own across the session: the harness recycling its own helpers. The 30s control was simply a quiet sample. Final proof with a stable population: locker killed 1 of 1, **0 of 16 unrelated killed**, node.exe written and unlocked; re-verified against the REAL install with a live sidecar running — exit 0, no dialog, 0 of 15 unrelated touched.
- **TRAP THAT DAMAGED THE MACHINE AND HAD TO BE REPAIRED: `/D=` DOES NOT ISOLATE THE REGISTRY.** Installing to a scratch dir with `/D=` correctly redirected the FILES, but the uninstall entry is keyed on the product, not the path — so the test install rewrote `HKCU\…\Uninstall\StarNet` to point at the temp dir, and cleaning that up deleted the REAL install's Add/Remove Programs registration. Repaired by re-running the installer against `%LOCALAPPDATA%\StarNet`, which rewrote the entry correctly (and doubled as the real-world test of the hook). **A `/D=` install is not a sandbox — budget for the registry side effect.**

So `checkpointStore`, constructed with `runGit: runGit`, was handed the wrong signature and **every `snapshot()` returned `null`**. Blast radius in the shipped app: every `shell.*` and `verify.*` tool call takes a checkpoint *regardless of the `CHECKPOINTS` flag* (`index.js:10714`) and `fs.write` takes one unconditionally (`index.js:11586`) — both inside swallow-all `try` blocks, so it failed in total silence; `GET /api/checkpoints` always listed nothing and RESTORE had nothing to restore. **Pre-existing: this shipped in v0.6.8.** Fixed at `3113523a` by renaming the checkpoint helper to `runGitCheckpoint` (one reference, the injection site; the night-shift name has ~30 call sites and was left alone).

**2026-07-27 merge digest (Hermes memory-parity: the four gaps):** `claude/starnet-hermes-memory-gaps-408646` -> `feat/harness-backend` merge `df7ae537` (snapshot `92a6f2a6`; code `a1fa9fdb`/`37059546`/`a4a72bcb`/`bd5ae899`, post-merge claims re-lock `b0610fc2`). Gate **test:fast 401 green + test:http green ON TRUNK**, claims planning authority **PASS** (181 locked paths, path set unchanged). Trunk was baselined **400 green at `92a6f2a6` BEFORE the merge**. Only ONE file overlapped trunk's 9 intervening commits — `qa/product-perfect/claims.json`, the expected re-lock collision, resolved to trunk and recomputed at the merge result because neither side's lock described the merged tree. No hotfile in my diff (trunk's `build.js`/`worldmodel.js`/`stationbake.js` changes are disjoint from mine and were `node --check`ed anyway), no `shared/`, no routes beyond one additive GET, no `package.json`, no credential moved. NOTE: another session merged the CONTROL FLOOR lane (`0ad324c1`) on top of this one mid-gate, which is why the step count reads 401; the first post-merge gate run showed a `spotify.store.test` D1 failure that did NOT reproduce in isolation and did NOT reproduce on a clean re-run — two concurrent `test:fast` runs in one integration tree race on shared scratch paths. **Closes the four gaps from the code-level re-audit against the reference harness.** (1) **recall_conversation only ever searched the OPEN workstream** — `transcriptstore.search()` hard-filtered one streamId, so an agent asked what was decided in another workstream answered "no messages match" while the answer sat on disk one stream over. It takes `scope:'all'` now, every hit carries its own streamId so a cross-stream quote is attributable, and two shapes reach parity with the reference harness's session search: `streams()` browses the workstreams that exist with a topic preview, `around(streamId, ts)` reads the turns surrounding a hit. **LAW: the anchor must be the TIMESTAMP** — a row index or synthetic id dies when `trimStreamRam()` splices rows out from under a drill-down, which is exactly when a drill-down is attempted. The tool infers its shape from its args and **AUTO-WIDENS a zero-hit stream search**, saying so; an explicitly pinned `scope:'stream'` never widens, because answering "we never discussed that" off a one-stream miss is the confidently-wrong claim this project treats as a defect. (2) **notebook.write was never dupe-checked** (reflection deduped its PROPOSALS by Jaccard since M-mem.6; the direct write path did not), so the same belief accumulated in a dozen phrasings, diluting top-K recall and leaving the Commander a panel of noise. The reference harness forces the issue with a hard char cap that ERRORS when full; we have no cap by design, so the equivalent is to stop the redundant write. **It CHALLENGES rather than blocks, and the reason is a real limit: token overlap cannot separate a restatement from two different facts sharing a shape** — "staging db is in frankfurt" vs "production db is in frankfurt" scores as high as a genuine paraphrase, because the one token carrying the difference is the one that differs. Any threshold tight enough to catch paraphrases will sometimes swallow a real memory, and a false suppression is worse than a duplicate. So the agent is shown the belief it already holds in full and decides: a restatement stops there, a genuinely distinct fact returns with `distinct:true` and saves. A challenged write **emits nothing** — no memory.write, no deliverable — because a receipt for a write that did not happen is a false claim. (3) **memory only formed on the WATCHED browser run.** `reflect:true` was set at exactly one call site, so cron fires, night shifts, workshop shifts, channel messages and the local OpenAI-compatible endpoint all did real work and threw away everything they learned. The rationale in the code ("only the WATCHED browser run reflects -> a turn-in beat") was true when reflection always raised a BLOCKING deck and stopped being true at the silent-save reversal. **The flag never meant "attended", it meant "this run did real work"** — it is set at every real-work host now. **Delegated workers deliberately stay OFF:** worker output returns as tool results inside the PARENT's messages, so the parent's reflection already covers them, and per-worker would pay N aux calls for one task and race N batches into one deck. Spend is bounded exactly as before (AuxGovernor budget, per-agent cooldown, salience gate all sit downstream of the flag). (4) Two things had to be true first. **ORIGIN:** records were keyed `notebook:<agent>` with no surface dimension, fine while every record was self-evidently the Commander's own conversation. `memcore.originOf` stamps `commander | channel:<name> | schedule | nightshift | api` at both write paths and the Memory Core shows a chip for everything except `commander` — the ordinary case stays quiet or the label becomes noise nobody reads. Channel DMs are owner-gated upstream (`adapter.js ownerOk`), so the real exposure was a whitelisted group chat. An untagged legacy record projects as `commander`, its only possible source. **DURABLE PENDING:** high-stakes proposals waited in an in-memory Map that died on restart and was reachable only by exact runId or a single newest-per-agent fallback, so a deck raised at 3am was a belief the Commander never got to rule on. `pending:<agent>` queues them durably with provenance (cap 50 FIFO, idempotent per `runId+":"+id` since every batch mints a prop_1), `GET /api/memory/pending` lists them across runs, a verdict arriving after a restart resolves against the QUEUE instead of 404-ing a real decision, and the new-hero reset wipes it so a re-commissioned hero inherits no stranger's deck. Live-verified on a booted seed station across a sidecar restart: origin chips render, the pending section shows the deck, **Keep drained the queue to 0, hid the section, took stored 3 -> 4, and landed the record on disk with `origin:'schedule'`, trust 0.3, and the sourceRunId of the run that PROPOSED it**. NOT verified: a real model calling recall_conversation cross-stream, and an unattended run reflecting end-to-end with a live provider — both need a key. **STILL OPEN, deliberately:** recall_conversation's reach is the RAM mirror (~1200 turns/stream via `ramPerStream`); older dialogue is on disk but unsearchable, where the reference harness searches its full SQLite DB via FTS5. Also **one source-lock law earned**: `sidecar.http.test.js` pinned the literal `if (prop.saved) return json(409` and broke on a rename while the guarantee was intact — **a needle must pin the GUARANTEE, not the variable name holding it**. The shipped ceiling made it reachable rather than theoretical: 20 min total (`CAPS.maxIters` x `toolTimeoutMs`) against 4 sequential workers each allowed 10 x 30s of tool time = exactly 20 min, **with zero headroom for model latency, which is most of the wall clock and appears nowhere in that formula**. LAW: **a wall clock derived from tool-timeout arithmetic is not a wall clock**, and **the mechanism that enforces a deadline must be the one that can still return partial work** — a registry-level timeout can only throw the results away. Each foreground worker now gets its own slice on its OWN abort controller chained to the parent (E-STOP still cascades, proven against a real `AbortController`), so a straggler is stopped ALONE and comes back as one honest `timeout` row carrying its partial text plus "do not present it as complete", while its siblings' results survive; sequential shares divide what is LEFT so a fast early worker donates its unused time, and the registry timeout is demoted to a backstop a minute above the budget. **Second: a parallel dispatch of 4 ran TWO at the shipped defaults.** The lead holds an admission slot for the entire dispatch and `MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS` is 3, so the gate refused the last two workers and **nothing ever retried them** — `maxWorkers` (4) simply exceeded the default fan-out capacity (2), and the lead synthesized a confident answer from half the crew's work. LAW: **a fan-out width that exceeds the admission gate's capacity is a silent-loss bug, not a queue** — refusal must never be the resting state of a requested worker. Both modes are one wave loop now (sequential = waves of 1, unchanged default; parallel = waves sized to the gate's LIVE free capacity, wired in from the host), a refusal from a race for the last slot is retried exactly once (a refused worker did no work and cost nothing), and a surviving refusal names `MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS` instead of blaming the model. **2026-07-26 merge digest (tool-schema cost lane):** `claude/starnet-hermes-parity-gaps-99c415` -> `feat/harness-backend` merge `ef522fa3` (snapshot `2b40689b`). Gate **test:fast 400 green + test:http green ON TRUNK**. No frontend/shared/package.json in the diff -> no claims re-lock, no golden. **The lane started from a measurement, not a hunch:** booting the real sidecar against a scripted mock and reading the wire showed a fully placed floor advertises **72 tools = 37.7KB = 59.7% of EVERY request**, re-sent on every turn (~1.5MB at maxIters=40) — and it was NOT mostly the browser (memory/skills averaged ~900 B/tool, routines/quests ~1,161). Ended at **53 tools / 29.7KB**. Four levers, in the order the measurement justified them. **(1) Prefix caching** `a7022b67`: Anthropic renders tools -> system -> messages and caches by PREFIX, so ONE `cache_control` breakpoint on the last system block covers the entire tool catalogue in front of it; a second rides the last message block. `cache_control` had been requested in exactly one place (openrouter's system message) while all four adapters READ `cached_tokens` back — a statistic we never asked for. **LAW THIS CREATES: the system prompt is now a CACHED PREFIX.** It works only because the prefix is byte-identical all run (loop.js resolves `tools` ONCE; `extractLeadingSystem` hoists only the LEADING system run, so mid-run `<steering_note>`/`<loop_guard>` land as USER turns) — **adding a clock, a turn counter or a remaining-budget line to the system prompt silently converts a 0.1x discount into a flat 1.25x surcharge, with no error.** Proven by driving the REAL loop 5 turns and diffing prefix bytes, with `<loop_guard>` observed riding the messages. **(2) The coupled honesty fix** `7d949555`, and it is not optional: `prices.js` had warned since it was written that folding cache traffic into prompt_tokens means "a heavily-cached run OVER-reports" — free advice while nothing requested caching. Measured once it did: **3.19x over-report, ~$1.62 of phantom spend per 40-turn run**, so the budget seatbelt fired that early. Cache ratios now ride the price object (anthropic 0.10x read / 1.25x write, gemini 0.25x); **a family with no entry keeps 1.0x so it can only ever OVER-report, never under** — the safe direction for a spend cap. Discount applies to DOLLARS ONLY; `prompt_tokens` stays the true count because the context gauges read it. **(3) tool.search** `aa0203bd`: a CAP_REGISTRY grant row may carry `deferred: true` — still GRANTED, just not advertised; the loop appends what the search finds for the rest of the run. **DEFERRAL IS ADVERTISING, NEVER CAPABILITY** — `resolveTools` still returns deferred tools in `tools`, so gate/consent/kill-switch are untouched, and `attenuate()` filters `deferred` by the same subset or a delegated worker could FIND what it may not run. **2026-07-25 merge digest (agent sprite smoothness):** `claude/agent-sprite-smoothness-981a49` -> `feat/harness-backend` merge `ce47789b` (snapshot `3751582f`), claims re-lock `ee7152ef`. Gate **test:fast 395 green ON TRUNK** + **GOLDEN PASS on trunk (17/17 within threshold, no re-bless owed)**. Frontend-only (no sidecar/routes/shared/package.json) -> no test:http.

**The user report:** agent sprites look "very 2D and not very smooth when they turn around", hypothesis "maybe we are lacking in frames". The hypothesis was WRONG and worth recording: frame count (6/dir) was never the problem, and the fix required no new art. Five causes, all in the movement/draw path: (1) `drawBody` rounded the body to integer WORLD units while the camera scales 0.5-6x, so a body sat still ~2 frames then hopped 2-6 DEVICE pixels — the loudest artefact, and note panX/panY were never rounded so the world was already sub-pixel while the body alone snapped; (2) facing was a bare `|dx|>|dy|` snap recomputed every frame, DUPLICATED IN THREE PLACES, so it strobed on near-45 headings and teleported the pose on a turn; (3) the walk cycle ran on the wall clock at fixed fps although pace is not fixed (crew temperament 0.88-1.17x, hero 34 u/s vs crew 28), so feet skated; (4) bodies went 0 -> full pace in one frame; (5) `path()` is a 4-NEIGHBOUR BFS, so every route was an orthogonal staircase and bodies **never moved diagonally at all**.

**Shipped:** device-pixel snap via `ctx.getTransform().a`; one `stepGait()` replacing all three facing snaps (continuous angle slewed at `TURN_RATE=12` rad/s, bucketed with `DIR_HYST=0.13` hysteresis); distance-phased stride on a `b.odo` odometer; speed easing (`ACCEL=150`) that brakes into the final stop only; and string-pulled paths in `worldmodel.js` behind a conservative `losClear` (every touched tile walkable, every orthogonal hop `canStep`-legal, diagonals demanding BOTH corners so a shortcut can never squeeze between two blockers). Waypoints also hand over `CORNER_LOOK=2.5` early and NO LONGER snap px/py onto the waypoint — that snap WAS the pivot.

**Two traps this lane paid for.** `b.phase` is DUAL-PURPOSE: `phaseOf()` indexes `PHASES[]` with it, so making it a float to de-sync the walk cycle returned `undefined` and killed the entire idle/mood engine on frame 1 — the float sprite offset is now a separate `aph`. And stride must never be a constant units-per-frame: **ULTRON ships 4 walk frames at 0.60 scale** where the other 38 sets use 6 at 0.36-0.425, so a fixed 3.4 spun his legs ~2.3x too fast; it is now DERIVED (`frameHeight * scale * 0.56 / fr.length`), which also makes any future skin correct with no retuning. Separately: a trailing `//` comment silently swallowed `pathPts/pathIdx/idleUntil/goal/say` off the crew spawn literal and `node --check` still passed — caught only by reading the SERVED file.

**Guard:** `test/path-smoothing.test.js` verifies the smoother INDEPENDENTLY of its own Bresenham walk — it samples every segment densely and asks `walkable()` about the tile under each sample. 1196 paths, 1712 diagonal segments (a 4-neighbour BFS produces zero), 8.1x waypoint compression, 0 wall violations. The gate meta-lint `lint-gate-can-fail` rejected its first version for lacking `A.report()`.

**Scope verified, not assumed:** exactly THREE movement sites exist in the codebase and all three now route through `stepGait`, and `SPRITES.drawBody` has exactly TWO callers (floor + static dossier portrait), so this covers all 39 skins plus ULTRON and future skins inherit it free. NOT automatic: 8-direction art — `DIR_A` has 4 entries and `pick()`'s fallback is 4 dirs. **DON'T buy diagonal art:** only 3 of 39 live sets have 8dir sources (`finn`/`caseyjones`/`pikachu`, the `*_v3` batch) because `_preset/preset.json` locks `n_directions: 4`; regenerating the other 36 is 540-900 generations against 219 remaining and would change their locked look. **OPEN:** Andrew has not yet judged the one real look change — diagonal MOVEMENT rendered with 4-direction art (the Stardew approach). Merge auto-merged cleanly against `c15960e0` (seat-centre); both sides verified present, all symbols defined exactly once.

# QA STATION — dashboard

**2026-07-26 merge digest (turf reads as grass):** `agent/turf-grass-mat` → `feat/harness-backend`, fast-forward to `f5bde64e` (snapshot `7eb53949`), claims re-lock `f5bde64e` carried from the lane and still valid (source `f1294c2b` ≠ HEAD). Gate **test:fast 399 green (exit 0) ON TRUNK**. Frontend-only → no test:http owed. Rides the next cut. Fast-forward, so no auto-merge touched the `worldmodel.js` hotfile; `node --check` + symbol counts verified anyway.

**The ask:** Andrew supplied a grass reference photo — "lets make our grass turf look more like the top left reference".

**The real defect was not the art, it was the RANDOMNESS.** v2 gave every blade an independent random tone off a 5-step ramp, so no pixel belonged to the pixel beside it — which is exactly why a field of grass read as static. Real grass clumps: a patch lights together and the gaps shadow together. Tone now comes from a two-octave value FIELD (~6px tufts over ~2px strands) sampled on ABSOLUTE bake-pixel coords, so neighbours share a tone, tufts continue across tile borders, and chunk↔monolithic parity still holds. Strands are lit one step off THEIR OWN tuft's tone rather than off a global ramp, so a blade always belongs to its clump. This generalises to any organic surface we add next (moss, sand, water, rust): **correlate, don't scatter.**

**Two tuning findings, both invisible without a render:** plain axis-aligned noise cells produced a QUILT OF SQUARES — right clump size, wrong shape, because every cell boundary lined up in both axes (cells are now sheared, x offset by a function of y); and amplitude ±0.20 read as camouflage blotches, legible clumps that stopped belonging to one surface (±0.13 with a dominant mid-tone reads as one lawn).

**Hue was fighting the material, and it was fixed by MEASUREMENT not by eye.** Grass is olive: red near green, blue well under both. `fern` (#2a3f24) is blue-leaning, and since `vivid()` drives the dominant channel hardest its lifts ran toward PURE green. Sampled channel ratios — reference ≈ R/G 0.83 · B/G 0.48; fern 0.62 · 0.51; new **`meadow` (#374024)** 0.83 · 0.50. A first cut at `#37401e` hit 0.83 · **0.41** and read as mustard: the blue channel is what separates grass from straw. TURF now `suggest`s meadow; existing rooms keep the hue they were built with, and HEDGE stays on fern (a bush is not a lawn).

**One deliberate law inversion:** dry blades use `U.shade`. The standing rule is never to `U.shade` anything that must KEEP its hue — a dead blade must LOSE it, and bleached straw is precisely desaturated-and-lighter, the direction `U.shade` travels.

**2026-07-25 merge digest (tool-RESULT injection defence):** `claude/routine-scheduled-runs-terminal-d179ff` -> `feat/harness-backend` merge `b64a875c` (snapshot `f622620c`). Gate **test:fast 398 green (exit 0) + test:http green (exit 0) ON TRUNK**, all three lanes re-proven live against the merged tree (taint 9/9, grant 14/14, prompt-guard 15/15).

**The gap.** The cron prompt scanner covers text the Commander wrote. It cannot see content the agent FETCHES mid-run — a hostile page, a compromised MCP server, a poisoned upstream result — and a granted routine auto-approves the terminal and connectors. Pattern-matching fetched content is the WRONG tool: it is arbitrary, and legitimate work constantly quotes attack commands (the exact false positive the cron-guard two-tier split exists to avoid).

**1. FENCE** (`sidecar/tools/fence.js`). web_* had fenced since the web lane; **browser page reads and MCP results did NOT** — the two newest untrusted sources arrived raw, and one of them (connectors) is what an unattended routine can now be granted. Extracted the shipped web fence VERBATIM into a shared module and wired browser (snapshot/get_text/console/dialog/vision) + MCP results to it. One marker pair, one scrub string: a second copy drifts, and a drifted scrub is a fence a hostile page can CLOSE. web.js behavior byte-identical (its own suite proves it).

**2. TAINT** (`sidecar/taint.js`). The structural half, because a fence is ADVISORY — it says what the content is, it cannot make the model obey. So the host removes the payoff instead of detecting the payload: once non-Commander content lands in an UNATTENDED run, that run loses `shell.exec`/`verify.run`, credential-spending `web_request`, and connector WRITES for the rest of the run. It does not matter what the injection says; the tools it needs are gone, and there is nothing to evade. **THE USABILITY LINE IS THE DESIGN** — connector READS, further web reads, jailed fs and memory all survive, or a routine whose job is "read three pages from one connector" dies on call two and the feature is worthless. Enforced pre-dispatch AND mirrored in the consent predicates from ONE shared definition, so gate and consent can never disagree. Autonomous only: a watched run has a human and live prompts, and removing powers mid-conversation would be hostile.

**Proven with the real attack**, not a simulation of one: a maximally credulous mock model (it ALWAYS obeys the page) reads hostile MCP text instructing it to run a command. The result arrives fenced, the injected `shell_exec` is BLOCKED, the refusal NAMES `mcp__notes__read_note`, and the command never runs — while a clean granted routine keeps its terminal and a tainted one keeps reading.

**LANE INTERACTION resolved** with the MCP result-cap lane that landed in parallel: the cap governs the SERVER's payload, the fence is host framing added on top (the same split web_fetch has always had), and **fencing happens AFTER clamping** — clamping a fenced string would slice the closing marker off a long result and hand the model an unterminated fence. Their two cap assertions were rewritten to assert the payload is byte-identical INSIDE the fence rather than that total content length equals the cap; the per-run tool-output budget still bounds the fenced total, so the context protection the cap exists for is intact. Browser conflicts combined rather than picked: iframe markers + fence on snapshot, and the vision `saved` note deliberately kept OUTSIDE the fence (host-authored provenance, not page content).

**Behavior change OUTSIDE this lane, flagged deliberately:** `web_request` is both a taint source (capability 'web') and revoked-when-tainted (`external-credentialed`), so on EVERY autonomous surface (cron, night shift, workshop, channels, openai-compat) it is now effectively single-use after any external read. That is intended — the per-key grant is per-KEY not per-HOST, the model picks the URL, so it is the most direct exfil channel — but it is a real reduction in another lane's shipped capability. One line in `allowedWhenTainted` if it needs narrowing.

**v1 boundaries, stated not hidden:** shell output and local fs reads do NOT taint (a granted routine's own `npm test` output would otherwise revoke its next command). A routine could still `cat` a downloaded file. Documented in the module header.

**TRAPS.** `SKYNET_ALLOW_LOOPBACK_FETCH` does not exist — I invented it; web_fetch to loopback is SSRF-refused (correct), so use an MCP connector as the offline taint source. A mock that DEDUPES tool messages fakes a "second connector read failed". Registry error results are prefixed `ERROR: ` so match block markers anywhere, not at index 0. **The interactive exemption could not be proven live headlessly** — web is SSRF-refused on loopback and MCP needs a live per-call confirmation — so it rests on the unit-asserted `surface !== 'interactive'` guard plus the autonomous positive proof. Verified NOT a bug while chasing one: connector tools persist fine across repeated runs (state stays `up`). No claims re-lock owed — the release surface is frontend/docs only (0 sidecar entries).

**2026-07-25 INCIDENT — a `git reset` on trunk silently deleted a merged lane, and the gate went GREEN over the hole.** Read this before the next merge. Sequence from `git reflog feat/harness-backend`: `@{7}` Tier-0 merged to trunk as `53bd090e` → `@{6}` another session committed a backdrop digest → `@{5}` **`reset: moving to 2bf21800`** → `@{4}` the digest re-committed → `@{3}` floor/wall merged → `@{1}` the honesty lane merged on top. The reset was almost certainly meant to undo only that session's own digest commit; it also discarded a merge that had landed in between, and every later merge was built on a trunk that had never contained Tier-0. **Net damage: `sidecar/providers/prices.js` (a SOURCE file), the truncated-stream fix in loop.js + all five providers, and 4 test files were absent from trunk while `test:fast` reported 387 steps GREEN** — the deleted tests took their own `fast.list` registrations with them, and a test that does not exist cannot fail. Caught only because the step count moved the WRONG WAY (387 where 389 was predicted: 386 base + 2 Tier-0 + 1 new). Recovered by re-merging the intact lane branch → `22679217`; all 4 tests registered and passing, `prices.js` restored, honesty lane preserved. **THREE LAWS: (1) `git reset` on trunk is never safe in a multi-session repo — `git revert` the specific commit instead; check `git log --oneline -3` first, another lane may have merged since you looked. (2) PREDICT the gate's step count before you run it and reconcile any difference — `lint-gate-can-fail` proves the REGISTERED steps can go red, it cannot prove the right steps are registered. The gate cannot detect its own amputation. (3) A green gate is evidence about the tree that was tested; after a concurrent merge or any history rewrite it is evidence about nothing.** Follow-up worth building: a guard asserting every `test/*.test.js` on disk appears in a list, so a vanished registration is loud.

  never drift.

  (`00b976506`, "the wall-mounted look was bad") because it LIFTED props onto the tall face the bake
  raises along a room's north edge. This version never lifts anything: it requires a wall north of
  every footprint tile and the prop draws exactly where it always did. One branch in `checkProp`,
  one catalog flag; the `propRules` injection already carried `mount` through.

two places; both were "both sides added new props at the same anchor" and were resolved by UNION,
with a duplicate-id check after (none).

metre. Two props in this lane shipped wrong before that was applied — the bench-press bar at
standing-head height, and rack weapons at 30px (86% of a person). ⛔ **AND WHEN A PROP CANNOT BE
BOTH TRUE-SCALE AND LEGIBLE, CUT THE COUNT, NOT THE SIZE**: two rifles and a blade at a truthful
18px are a texture; one rifle at 22px with a blade on its own shelf reads.

here affects the already-packaged installer: no version file is touched and no existing prop art
changed. A station saved WITH these props and opened by the shipped build loses them, since
`deserialize` prunes prop types the running build does not know.

## 2026-08-17 — RECLINER (merged `f860b8797`, pure FF)

One seat of the couch, shipped as TWO lounge props: `recliner` faces left, `recliner_r` faces right.
Every other seat in the catalog faces the camera, which is half of why a furnished room reads as a
showroom row.

- `recliner_r` is not a second drawing — it calls `F.recliner` under an integer horizontal mirror,
  and `px()` re-maps the directional tones through a new `LSWAP` table so the warm KEY stays
  high-west where the ceiling strip is instead of riding round with the furniture. One drawing, two
  props, no drift.
- ⛔ **THE OUTLINE MUST OPEN.** Two drafts drew a filled rounded box and both read as an appliance.
  A seat seen from the side is a C: the arms reach further forward than the cushion between them and
  the back stands proud of both. Those notches ARE the silhouette; shading changes nothing until
  they exist. The arms must also STOP at the back — run them the full width and they paint over its
  crown, leaving a stack of horizontal bands.
- ⛔ The art overhangs its tile 3px each side (a seat is deeper than one tile); what it BLOCKS is
  still the honest 1x1.
- ⛔ **MERGE ORDER IN `px`:** the mirror swap picks a different AUTHORED tone, then the local-colour
  dial grades whatever was picked. Grading first would hand `LSWAP` a colour that is not in its
  table. That union is the resolution of the one real conflict with the CHROMA lane.

**Gate:** `npm run test:fast` **643/643 green FROM THE LOG** on the synced lane tree, hash-identical
to trunk by the FF.

## Green Guardian (lane Q1)

One cycle = pin trunk into a **dedicated** checkout and run the four detectors against it:
`test:fast` → `shoot` → `golden` → `audit`. One deduped ledger finding per regression
(fingerprinted per failing suite/frame/assertion so the same defect never re-nags), the
row above refreshed, nonzero exit on any red. Run it:

```
npm run qa:guardian            # one cycle; exits nonzero if trunk is red/blocked
npm run qa:guardian -- --skip-visual   # test:fast + audit only (no Chrome; CI-lite)
npm run qa:guardian:watch      # poll trunk HEAD; run a cycle when it moves
```

**Pinned checkout (read-only law).** Gates NEVER run in the integration tree or another
agent's worktree. The Guardian owns a detached `git worktree` at `../_qa-guardian-pin`
(override with `SKYNET_GUARDIAN_PIN`), `git reset --hard`'d to the current trunk head each
cycle (created + `npm install`'d on first run). Sidecar/CDP ports stay in the Guardian
range: shoot `8940/9340`, golden `8941/9341`, audit `8942/9342`.

**STATUS.md + findings target the guardian's OWN repo, not the pin.** The row above and
`qa/findings/*.json` are written into the qa/ dir of the repo the guardian *script* lives
in (resolved from `import.meta.url`), so the dashboard reflects live state and survives the
pinned checkout's next `reset --hard`. Evidence (logs, flagged golden PNGs, gate reports)
is copied into `.bugloops/guardian-<stamp>/` for the same reason. Findings are filed
through `scripts/qa/ledger.mjs --add` so dedup / known-refusal stays the ONE implementation.

**No-fake-green.** A step that cannot run (git/npm/spawn failure, timeout, missing report)
files a **P0 BLOCKED** finding loudly and the cycle exits nonzero — it never silently
passes. Scheduling (Task Scheduler vs. a `/loop` session) is lane Q5's job; this script is
schedule-agnostic.

**Dismissed-frame gate (golden).** A golden frame whose *current* fingerprint is already
**dismissed/known** in the ledger is **review-clean**, not a regression: `scripts/golden.mjs`
asks the ledger's `suppressedFingerprints()` (the ONE dedup/known authority) and computes each
frame's Green-Guardian fingerprint (`goldenFrameFingerprint(name)` == `fingerprintOf({crew:'Green
Guardian', checkId:'golden', subject:'frame/'+name})`). A match is logged as `review-clean …
matches dismissed finding <fp>` and kept OUT of `flagged`, so golden exits 0 and the row above
stays GREEN. This exists because `sys-rewind` (the one modal that doesn't full-bleed over the
animated CRT floor) diffs forever as animation noise — its finding `01c40465` was triaged and
**dismissed**, yet a naïve golden gate would re-flag it every cycle and pin this row RED with 0
open findings (a lying dashboard). **Narrow by design:** only a frame whose fingerprint is on the
dismissed/known baseline is excused; a new frame, a different frame, or a diff on a non-dismissed
frame STILL flags → exit 3 → the Guardian files it through the ledger exactly as before. Fail-open:
if the ledger can't be read, nothing is suppressed. Covered by `test/golden.test.js`.

## Ledger quick reference

```
# file a finding (rejected without evidence; refused if known/dismissed; deduped by fingerprint)
node scripts/qa/ledger.mjs --add --json '{"crew":"Green Guardian","severity":"P0","title":"...","detail":"...","evidence":["path/to/artifact"],"checkId":"...","subject":"..."}'

# morning report (grouped by severity then crew); --write persists to qa/digests/<date>.md
node scripts/qa/ledger.mjs --digest [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--write]

# is this fingerprint already filed / known?
node scripts/qa/ledger.mjs --dedup-check <fingerprint>

# per-crew roll-up (the table above, live)
node scripts/qa/ledger.mjs --status
```

(1) MISFIRE POLICY — a recurring fire past its grace window now consults job.misfire ('fire_once' collapses the missed backlog into ONE catch-up run, default for cron schedules + intervals >=1h; 'skip' = old behavior, default for fast intervals) so opening StarNet at 12:01 no longer silently loses the 9:00 routine; additive/editable field, normalized in the store. (2) TRANSACTIONAL DISPATCH — a launch is conditional on a verified durable advance/claim: index.js setJobs returns an honest receipt (false = write never hit disk, RAM mirror rolled back to disk state so jobs stay due); the driver fires NOTHING over a failed receipt (all planned fires defer, retry next tick). (3) GENERATION FENCE — only the run still owning its lease may markRun; a zombie-swept run settling late can no longer overwrite the replacement's record (emits cron.result tagged 'stale-lease' instead). (4) TICKER HEALTH + DELIVERY OUTCOMES — GET /api/cron carries additive health {lastTickAt,lastSuccessAt,lastTickError,healthy = armed AND clean tick within 3 periods}; autonotify send attempts report per-send outcomes, {ok:false} SendResults normalized to real failures, persisted as lastDeliveryAt/Ok/Error via the new markDelivery reducer. New test/cron.dispatch.test.js (21 assertions, fast gate) locks fail-then-recover exactly-once + replacement-record survival + fenced abort. Live-proven on a real booted sidecar (isolated ws, zero spend): health real+healthy over HTTP, 3h-stale daily PLANNED AS FIRE (no-capability at the gate, no caught-up skip), nextRunAt fast-forwarded, legacy jobs load fine. - 2026-07-25: API-CONNECTION GAP — three stacked lanes (`claude/api-connection-p0` → `claude/web-request-tool` → `claude/connect-platform-catalog`) -> trunk merge `586e7acb` (snapshot `39afdf06`), re-locks `481eab54` / `87c9f9ea`. From a user report that Printify would not connect; NOTHING shipped is Printify-specific — other harnesses have no Printify-specific code either, they just have a generic path that works, and that is what was missing. **(1) KEYS-tab keys NEVER reached an agent's shell:** `servicekeys.deriveEnvVar` always ends `_API_KEY` and `environment.sanitizeChildEnv` strips every `*_KEY`/`*_TOKEN`, so 100% of pasted keys were scrubbed from the child env while `promptBlock` still told the model "available to your shell commands ... call that service's API directly (curl etc.)" — the model expanded an empty string and got a 401. Broke EVERY platform, not just POD. Fixed with a per-call `serviceEnv` hook (`servicekeys.runEnv`), deliberately NOT a boot snapshot: a key pasted after boot is live on the very next run, a disabled one gone on the very next run. Provider/billing keys stay reserved and still never reach a child. The comment that caused it claimed shell children "inherit" `process.env` — they do not; corrected in place. **(2) The MCP STDIO tab could never connect:** `makeStdioTransport` requires `deps.userControlIsolated === true`, which appears in exactly THREE places repo-wide (the check plus two lines in `test/mcp.stdio.test.js`) and is set NOWHERE in production; the installed app also pins `STARNET_MCP_STDIO=0` (`src-tauri/src/main.rs`, locked by `test/tauri.hardening.test.js`). The pane offered command/args/cwd/env and advertised seven launchers anyway, saved the config ENABLED, and the doomed row was retried every boot forever. The mark is CLIPPED under the windows instead: new `frontend/app/logoclip.js` (`LogoClip.clipFor`) subtracts the visible window rects from the mark's box and emits the `clip-path` for what survives. **Subtracting the REAL rects, not hiding the mark on first contact** — a window's left edge cuts the wordmark exactly where the edge lands, which is what makes it read as occlusion rather than a logo popping out. Driven from ONE `MutationObserver` on `#terms`: childList = open/close, `style` = drag/resize/`placeTerm`, `class` = minimize/restore, plus `animationend` for the `term-power` scale (which moves no attribute and so fires no mutation of its own). **uiZoom law** — rects are VISUAL px, `clip-path` coordinates are the element's own LAYOUT px, divided exactly once inside `clipFor`. **A fully-buried mark emits `inset(50%)`, never `path("")`**: an empty path string is invalid CSS, the declaration would be dropped, and the logo would land back on top — the original bug wearing a fix. **VERIFIED VISUALLY, before/after, on one seeded station** over headless CDP (`scripts/lib/cdp.mjs`), the "before" produced by neutralising `LogoClip.clipFor` in-page so both frames are the same build: SETTINGS parked at x=96 against a mark at x=32 gives `path("M 0 0 H 68.14 V 23.99 H 0 Z")` — 78.36 visual px / 1.15 station zoom = 68.14 layout px, so "STAR" survives and "NET" is gone, and the surviving part keeps its full above-the-glass crispness. ## 2026-07-29 — offline Local Live voice made honest (agent/local-voice-honesty → dfa761c2)

Merged `3c6c5b0d` (fix) + `34d289c2` (claims re-lock) into trunk `957592b0` as `dfa761c2`. Full
`npm test` on trunk after the merge: **NPM_EXIT=0 read FROM THE LOG**, `run-fast-tests: OK — 449
step(s) green`, whole http/e2e chain green, zero FAIL lines. Merge was clean (no conflicts); all
five touched JS files pass `node --check` and every symbol in `sidecar/local-voice.js`
(`installed`/`requireInstalled`/`packagePresent`/`status`/`warm`/`transcribe`/`synthesize`/
`defaultCacheRoot`) is defined exactly once with `module.exports` intact.

THE DEFECT: the first `dependencies` block in this repo's history landed after the v0.7.0 tag
(`@huggingface/transformers` + `kokoro-js` → onnxruntime native binaries) to power offline speech.
But `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` ships only `../sidecar`, `../frontend`, `../shared` as bundle
resources and **no node_modules**, `main.rs` describes a "zero-dependency Node sidecar", and
`release-cut.mjs` runs no install into the bundle — so those imports can never resolve in an
installed build. `status()` nevertheless hardcoded `available: true`, so the always-visible
top-bar mic button opened the user's microphone, claimed "Downloading or loading local speech
models", and then painted a raw `Cannot find module '@huggingface/transformers'` into the panel.
`test/local-voice.test.js` asserted `available === true` and exercised only `transcribe(silence)`,
which short-circuits on an RMS gate BEFORE any dynamic import — so it stayed green in a tree where
neither package was installed at all, which is the state of every shipped build.

THE FIX: probe both packages on disk (`require.resolve`, treating `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`
/ `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM` as proof-of-presence since an ESM-only exports map refuses the CJS condition
only after reading package.json, plus a `module.paths` directory walk) and report `available` +
`reason` truthfully; report `asr`/`tts` as `unavailable` rather than `cold`, which promises a
warm-up that will never come; `warm`/`transcribe`/`synthesize` reject with a tagged error and the
routes answer **501** (not a 202 that cannot be honoured, nor a 503 that invites a retry);
`transcribe` refuses AHEAD of the silence gate, because an empty transcript reads as "you said
nothing" — a claim a build with no ASR cannot make; the panel checks availability BEFORE opening
the microphone and offers no RETRY affordance; the model cache moves to the documented data root
(`%LOCALAPPDATA%\StarNet\models`, `~/Library/Application Support/StarNet` on macOS) instead of a
stray `~/Starnet`; and the test now derives its expectation from disk and holds BOTH contracts.

VERIFIED LIVE, not inferred: both probe directions proven by stubbing the two packages in and out
(absent → `available:false`; present → `available:true`/`cold`/silence `''`). Against a real
sidecar on a scratch workspace: `GET /api/local-voice/status` 200 `available:false`, `POST
/api/local-voice/warm` **501**, `POST /api/local-voice/transcribe` **501** with the clean message.
Browser DOM round-trip on the served page: panel state `UNAVAILABLE`, model row `LOCAL MODELS: NOT
INSTALLED`, retry hidden, `aria-pressed=false` — **the microphone is never opened**. Blast radius
was only the Local Live mic: `preferLocalTts` defaults false and the TTS route falls through to
the cloud provider chain, so no existing user's voice was affected.

GATE HONESTY: the first run of this branch came back **RED** — `qa-product-perfect-claims.test.js`,
9 problems. Rather than assume it was ambient churn, the test was run at the fork point in a
`worktree add --detach` probe, where it **passed (64 assertions)** — so the failure was mine:
`frontend/app/voice-live.js` is in the 189-file measured surface. Re-locking with
`claims.mjs --refresh-surface` fixed only 2 of the 9 until the lock was COMMITTED, since the ledger
reads the commit and not the working tree; committed, the suite returns 64/64. Surface count stayed
189 → 189, so this lane added no file to the measured set.

## 2026-07-30 — Local Live voice: the keyless ladder that nothing was calling

Merged `agent/voice-listen-fallback` as `4bda2886` (+ notes/lock `9107ad8f`, claims re-lock). Full
`npm test`: **NPM_EXIT=0 read FROM THE LOG, `run-fast-tests: OK — 462 step(s) green`**, zero FAIL.
Merge clean, all four files `node --check` clean, both website mirrors byte-identical to source, and
`function start` appearing twice was a grep artifact (`startDictation`), not merge damage.

THE REPORT WAS "voice mode says nothing is available, it should use the model." The honest chain
behind it, each link verified rather than assumed:

1. **Local Live listened only through the offline models.** Its own mic capture →
   `/api/local-voice/transcribe` → Whisper, which needs `@huggingface/transformers` + `kokoro-js`.
   The Tauri bundle ships `sidecar/`, `frontend/`, `shared/` and **no node_modules**, confirmed by
   inspecting the staged resource in the build. So it could never listen in an installed copy.
2. ⛔ **A KEYLESS LADDER FOR EXACTLY THIS CASE EXISTED AND NOTHING CALLED IT.**
   `nativeSpeechProvider` → `POST /api/stt/native` (Windows System.Speech, no key, pure PowerShell,
   ships inside the bundle) is selected **only** inside `startCoordinator` — and `startCoordinator`
   was **exported and never invoked by any frontend file**. Local Live called `attachCoordinator`,
   which registers state hooks and never selects an stt provider. ⛔ **An exported function with no
   caller is dead code, and `grep -c` on the export list will not tell you** — grep the call sites.
3. **Speaking was never broken.** `edgetts.js` is a free keyless neural floor, on unless
   `STARNET_EDGE_TTS` is off. The report named "voice" but only listening was down.
4. **The user's premise was wrong in a checkable way, and checking it mattered.** A ChatGPT sub
   cannot drive this: `TTS_KEY_PROVIDERS = ['openrouter','gemini','openai']` excludes codex, and the
   `marin` realtime path resolves `providerRuntimeKey('openai')` with its own error string "OpenAI
   API key required for live voice" — and has **no UI wiring at all** (`/api/realtime/*` is called by
   zero frontend files). ⛔ **Three speech backends existed; the button reached one.**
5. ⛔ **MY OWN EARLIER GREP WAS WRONG AND NEARLY FROZE A FALSE CONCLUSION.** I searched
   `api/native-stt`; the routes are `/api/stt/native/status` and `/api/stt/native`. The wrong path
   returned zero hits and I reported the fallback as entirely uncalled. **Confirm a route's real
   path from the route table before concluding "nothing calls it."**

THE FIX: when the models are absent, probe `/api/stt/native/status` and run dictation mode through
`startCoordinator`; leave local TTS OFF there so speech takes the Edge floor; refuse honestly only
when neither leg exists.

⛔ THREE BUGS CAUGHT IN MY OWN FIX BY VERIFYING IT LIVE, NOT BY READING IT:
- **The label lied.** It said `WINDOWS DICTATION` unconditionally, but in a browser the same ladder
  picks the browser engine. Now read back from a new `Voice.sttEngine()`. ⛔ **And my guess at the
  provider id (`'web'`) was wrong — it is `'web-speech'` — which rendered "ASR UNKNOWN" in the live
  DOM. A label that names an engine must READ the selection, never re-derive it.**
- **A bogus reconnect.** Dictation mode holds no browser stream, so the `visibilitychange` /
  `devicechange` handlers read `stream == null` as "microphone lost" and fired a reconnect that would
  seize the very device this mode must not touch. ⛔ **`active` is not one state — a second mode
  under the same flag inherits every guard written for the first.**
- **A leaked listen loop.** Teardown detached the hooks but never stopped the coordinator, so the
  sidecar kept being asked to dictate after the panel closed. `stopCoordinator` on finish.

VERIFIED LIVE: panel opens to `listening` with `ASR BROWSER SPEECH · VOICE EDGE`, no error row; the
sidecar reports `{"available":true,"engine":"windows-system-speech"}`; closing leaves
`inVoiceMode:false` / `isListening:false`. ⛔ **NOT VERIFIED: a real Windows-dictation utterance
end-to-end.** The browser pane HAS SpeechRecognition, so it exercised the `web-speech` leg; the
`native` leg is selected only where SR is absent, i.e. the packaged WebView2 shell. Driving
`/api/stt/native` by hand opens the operator's real microphone for 15s, so it was left for the
installed test rather than done unasked.

ALSO FOUND, NOT A VOICE BUG: the awakening re-ran on every fresh client because
`needsAwakening = !agent.onboarded` and the station save carried `onboarded: false`. Patched on a
THROWAWAY COPY only to get a past-onboarding dev server; the live station was not touched. ⛔ **And
a dev sidecar is the wrong place to sign into Codex: OAuth refresh rotation means two clients on one
ChatGPT session consume each other's tokens, so signing in there can log the installed app out.**
The "We couldn't authorize this device" message is **OpenAI's own copy** — that string exists nowhere
in this repo — and pending device logins live in an in-memory `Map`, so **restarting the sidecar
voids an in-flight sign-in**. RELEASE_NOTES.md was rewritten: it had claimed the panel simply
refuses, which stopped being true the moment this landed.

## 2026-07-30 — the voice fallback fired agent runs from room noise (my regression, gated)

Merged `agent/voice-noise-gate` as `ba323292`. Full `npm test`: **NPM_EXIT=0 read FROM THE LOG,
`run-fast-tests: OK — 462 step(s) green`**, zero FAIL.

⛔⛔ **WIRING DEAD CODE INHERITS ITS UNTESTED FLAWS.** The previous digest wired
`nativeSpeechProvider` because it had no caller. It also had no noise gate — harmless while nothing
invoked it, a live defect the moment something did. The leg turned **any** non-empty transcript into
a full agent run, and a `DictationGrammar` answers a cough or a fan with a real-looking short word.
**Proven from the user's own workspace, not theorised:** `runs.jsonl` carried a COMPLETED run
`{"reason":"done","turns":1,"tokens":10706,"title":"Mm."}` — ten thousand tokens spent on a noise
burst — and the diagnostics showed **five provider failures in 50 seconds**, an unattended burst that
earned a genuine upstream rate-limit. **The Whisper path never had this problem because it gates on
audio energy (`rms < 0.0025`) before transcribing; the native leg had no gate at all.**

THE FIX: capture System.Speech's own `Confidence` (it was being thrown away — the script read only
`$x.Text`) and threshold it, plus drop non-lexical noise tokens and punctuation-only text.
⛔ **Confidence crosses the wire as an INTEGER PER-MILLE on purpose: PowerShell's `{0:N3}` is
culture-sensitive, so a decimal-comma machine emits "0,842" and every parse of it reads as 0 —
silently muting the entire gate on exactly the machines hardest to debug.** A missing separator means
UNKNOWN confidence, never zero, so an older or future script cannot have every utterance dropped.
A dropped utterance returns `ok:true` with empty text and **no `error` field**, which the caller
already reads as "silence, listen again" — an `error` there would paint a red failure for a quiet
room. It composes with the pre-existing `MAX_EMPTY = 3`, so a noisy room now ends with a **cold mic
and "tap 🎤 when ready"** instead of a burst of runs. Real one-word commands ("stop", "yes") still pass.

⛔ **DIAGNOSING THIS REQUIRED ABANDONING TWO WRONG THEORIES, AND BOTH LOOKED GOOD ON PAPER.**
(1) "codex cannot serve `gpt-5.6-sol`" — the model appears nowhere in the repo and `CODEX_MODELS`
excludes it, which read as conclusive. It was wrong: the user round-tripped the model and the same
slug worked. ⛔ **The give-away I ignored: the failure arrived as an SSE `error` EVENT mid-stream, not
an HTTP status — an unservable model would have been a 400 on the status path.** (2) `ratelimits.js`
caching a per-model cooldown — refuted by its own header ("a pure store… decides nothing and blocks
nothing") and by the diagnostics line saying no quota headers were ever observed.
**What settled it was reading `runs.jsonl` and `diag.errors.json` out of the live workspace.**
⛔ **LAW: when a provider error resists two good theories, stop reasoning about the request and read
the run records.**

STILL TRUE AND STILL UNFIXED, worth its own lane: the station save carries **two disagreeing values
for the same setting, twice** — `doc.prov: "codex"` vs `agent.provider: "openrouter"`, and
`doc.reasoningEffort: "high"` vs `agent.reasoningEffort: "medium"`. Resume only fills a value when one
is MISSING (`if (!agent.provider && saved.prov)`), so it never reconciles a conflict, and which value
takes effect depends on which path reads it. That split-brain is why a manual model round-trip
"fixed" things — it rewrote both sides. ⛔ **Also: `agent.save.json` was still stamped 21:17 the
previous evening while the app ran, so an in-app settings fix had not reached disk and a restart
would resume the failing combination.**

2026-08-03 merge: agent/toast-compact -> feat/harness-backend (pure FF `11da64b2`..`78ff7c8e`) — the readout card, reviewed live by Andrew, taken down a size: card height 43→35px, rack 392→356px, value 15→13px, blade 26→22px, label/stamp 10→9px, ticks 6→5px, gap 7→6px. 356px is a FLOOR, not taste: below it ordinary prose wraps, and a wrapped compact card is TALLER than the roomy one it replaced. The size sweep also exposed a real geometry bug PREDATING the redesign — `#toast-stack` is a `body` child so TEXT SIZE's body zoom multiplies into it, but the things it is parked between (CREW rail, COMMS, dock) are cabinet, counter-zoomed to a fixed visual size by `--cz`. A flat `left: 268px` therefore walked the rack deeper into the stage at every text step while the gap never moved: measured at 1024×768 the OLD rack ran to x718 with COMMS starting at x668 — 50px under the live conversation. Fixed by writing the anchor and the space cap in hardware units (`calc(268px * var(--cz))`, `min(356px, calc(37vw * var(--cz)))`) while the 356px design width stays content-scaled: the card's TYPE is what you read and still grows with the dial; where it sits and how much room it may claim do not. Below 1120px the cabinet stops counter-zooming entirely (app.css narrows the grid with no `* var(--cz)`), so at a big text scale COMMS swells across the stage and no cap on our side helps — from that breakpoint the rack parks in the left gutter, the move the layout already makes at 900px (a transient card over the CREW list beats one over the live conversation). Verified live over CDP against a seeded worktree sidecar, 7 geometry cases (1440/1280/1024/880 × text 100/115/130/150) asserting per case that the rack stays in the viewport, clear of COMMS, and that no message is clipped or runs under the stamp: ALL PASS (1/7 failed before the fix), console clean. Look re-confirmed at the compact size across all five severities, labeled/unlabeled/wrapping/actionable, amber + green themes, and `prefers-reduced-motion`; longest real notify() literal in the app (120 chars, stationui.js) wraps to 3 lines cleanly. Gates FROM THE LOGS: lane fast 511 green pre-merge; trunk post-merge fast 511 green, 0 FAIL lines. ⛔ Harness trap for the next agent: stationui re-runs `applySettings()` on resize whenever textScale is AUTO, so writing `body.style.zoom` and THEN firing a resize silently reverts it to the auto value — an entire sweep read `zoom=1.15` for every case and looked like it had tested HUGE when it had tested nothing. Let the viewport override's own resize settle first, then write, and fire no further resize.

2026-08-03 merge: agent/summon-desk-beat -> feat/harness-backend (merge `f570db16`, lane commits `41980ba2` + in-lane claims re-lock `f755a253`) — THE POST-SUMMON DESK STEP IS NOW OWNED BY THE NEW AGENT'S SESSION. Reported by Andrew: summoning an agent from the Recruitment Bay opened its session with nothing but the generic starter hint — no instruction to place its workstation, no chip to do it. Reproduced live over CDP against a seeded worktree sidecar: on a quiet floor the line DID still print at summon, but `Chat.localLine` writes a DOM row only, and `load()` rebuilds a stream's log from `ws.history` — so switching to any other stream and back, or reloading, erased the only place the required step was ever stated (measured: `deskLine:true` at summon -> `false` after one switch, `false` after reload). The old block also stood down on `Chat.beatBusy()` and never queued, so any live beat elsewhere dropped it outright. FIX: the prompt is a property of the STREAM, not a one-shot print. `chat.js maybeDeskPrompt()` runs inside `load()` (right after the empty-state hint) and asks the new `App.needsWorkstation(agentId)` — a truthful read of the LIVE FLOOR (is any prop whose capability is `computer` bound to this agent?), never a stored flag — so the line plus its `▤ PLACE ITS DESK` chip stand on EVERY open of that session until the desk exists and vanish for good the moment it does; 'later' dismisses the view, never the owed step. The chip still opens REFIT armed on the PROP tool / WORKSTATIONS category, so the next floor click drops the desk. The hero is excluded (its starter desk is seeded at wake, and its stream owns the first-run hint), an agent whose desk came with it (the overseer's `team.summon`, `opts.desk`) is never told it has nowhere to sit, and a missing station fails CLOSED rather than claim a floor state the harness cannot prove. `summonAgent`'s own copy of the line + chips is deleted — one source. Files: `frontend/app/app.js`, `frontend/app/chat.js`, new `test/summon-desk-prompt.test.js` (+17 assertions, added to `test/fast.list`), website mirror synced, claims re-locked in-lane. Verified live over CDP on the exact merged code, 10/10 green: hero stream not nagged · summon opens the new agent's session focused and stating the step with the chip · still there after switch-away-and-back · still there after a full reload · the chip opens REFIT with prop tool + workstation category both active · once `ensureWorkstation` places the desk the prompt is gone · console clean. **2026-08-04 merge digest (SEAT LAW):** `agent/seat-law` -> trunk (merge `324d508b`, claims re-lock `e29c97c3`). Reported by Andrew from a screenshot: an idle agent drew its chair-sit pose on the BED — `planBedSleep` rendered the body on the mattress with `sitting = true`, so a dormant agent read as parked bolt-upright on the bunk; couch and beanbag carried the same `sit: true`. **The law: the sit sprite is a CHAIR pose, so `use.sit` may only be true where a seat is really under the body** — now exactly two catalog rows, STOOL and CHAIR (`kind: 'seat'`, previously not sittable at all). New `planSeat` claims one, walks the body to an adjacent tile, renders it ON the seat tile, and the seated y-sort inverts (`seatPy - 1`, was `+ 1`: the old `+1` existed so a sofa's back panel could occlude a couch sitter). Two bugs caught by live verification, not by tests: (1) `takeSeat()` left `seated` true when a claim has no cushion, so a body that got off a stool drew itself back at the stool — a claim is a reservation, not a place to render; (2) an abandoned seat plan's stale `pendSeat` was consumed by the NEXT goal's arrival, so `planSeat`/`planCouchSit`/`planBedSleep` now `releaseSeat()` before claiming (latent before this lane — every prop used to set a pendSeat, so the wrong one still landed the body on something plausible). `test/propanchor.test.js` now walks the WHOLE catalog, so a future `sit: true` on some new sofa fails the gate instead of shipping. New `World._dbgArrive()` runs the arrival beat on demand — the pose is decided in `arrive()`, and a verify script cannot wait out a walk when the rAF loop is frozen (an undisplayed preview pane composites no frames). Live-proven on the merged trunk tree (seeded worktree sidecar :9505, DOM round-trips, no JS exceptions): stool + chair -> `sitting:true seated:true` rendering exactly on the seat tile; bed, couch/lounge, beanbag, and the bedless power-down -> `sitting:false seated:false` on their own tile; never more than one seat claim held. **2026-08-05 merge digest (SPRITE WALK TRACKS):** `agent/sprite-fix` -> trunk (merge `ddd60f89`, base `5da06427`). Andrew: "pikachu and skeleton are not consistent in frames and pikachu lacks proper walking animations now" — two SEPARATE defects, both introduced by the 8-direction rebuild, both invisible to the file-level checks. (1) SKELETON's walk came back rendered 28-38% LARGER than its rotations in all eight directions; `assemble8.py` foot-anchors every frame independently, so it accepted that silently — the frames all sit on the floor line, they are just a different build, and the body grew a third the moment it stepped. Measured against the roster: max(walk content h)/rot h is 0.96-1.08 across the healthy 36 sets, skeleton was 1.28-1.38. NEW `_assembly/fit_walk_to_idle.py` applies ONE factor per direction about the foot anchor, so the cycle's own stride survives untouched and only the build moves — now 1.013. (2) PIKACHU's walk template needs legs to SWING and its feet never separate, so Pixellab returned six near-copies of the standing pose: frame-to-frame change was the roster's LOWEST (0.31 vs a 0.44-0.86 band) and all of it was outline noise, which is why it both shimmered and slid. NEW `_assembly/bob_walk.py` builds the bob `assets.js` already documents these sets as having (see CYCLE_PER_HEIGHT), keying the cycle off the MEDOID frame per direction so the noise is dropped rather than averaged, driven by squash/stretch/lift about the planted foot; steps 1 and 2 are now byte-identical (shimmer gone) with ~7% of drawn height in head travel. Neither set changes which gait path assets.js takes: pikachu's foot band still beats its idle by only 2px, under the 3px threshold that keeps it on the documented fallback constant, and skeleton keeps its measured stride, now scaled with the body instead of over-striding. A LEAN (rotating the body a few degrees) was built and REJECTED on inspection: at scale 0.36 (~19 device px) 1.5deg moves an ear tip half a pixel and all it buys is a full-body rotate resample that softens every frame against the crisp untouched idle. NEW `dev/walkbuild.mjs` is the proof instrument, reading build ratio + head-lift + foot-swing off the shipped `SPRITES.drawBody` on a transparent field, and it is verified in BOTH directions: on the PRE-FIX art it FAILS (skeleton 1.279, pikachu 1/2 quarter-px against bars of 6/12), on the fixed art it passes (skeleton 1.044, pikachu head bob 10 qpx), with the endoskeleton/secretagent controls unmoved at 1.000 either way. Three traps that cost a round each: drawBody loads a set LAZILY and returns null on the first call for a cold set (a probe measuring on first call measures nothing, for every set); asserting head movement on EVERY set fails the healthy controls because a stride moves the legs and leaves the head put; and at ~19 device px a real bob and a frame of generation noise are both "1px", so the probe draws through a 4x setTransform (drawBody snaps to the DEVICE pixel, so this sharpens rather than blurs). Gates FROM THE LOGS: lane fast **534/534**; trunk post-merge fast **535/535** green. Claims untouched (sprite PNGs are not in the measured surface; planning PASS 204 files throughout). NOTE: the lane's first gate failed on qa-product-perfect-claims naming `frontend/app/voice.js` — a file the lane never touched — because the worktree had branched off `a27db65c`, which trunk no longer contains; rebasing onto real trunk cleared it. Pixellab quota is SPENT (0 generations, 3948/3935 used, $4.07 credits), so a real limb-swing regen for pikachu needs a top-up.

Not art — a CONTRACT DRIFT. `worldmodel` opens an auto-door at EVERY orthogonally adjacent tile pair of two different zones (the foundation default that lets rooms connect with no door tool), so the `door` flag quietly stopped meaning "a doorway" and came to mean "these two zones touch here" — and FOUR paint passes written against the old meaning each laid their doorway dressing down the WHOLE shared boundary: `bakeThreshold`'s recessed `#3a352c` track + lit lip (from both sides), `bakeDeck`'s pale guide ticks, a gloss sheen dab per `doorDefs` pair, and a bright `LIGHT.door` cut in the ambient mask. Measured off the seam line itself, so it scales with the station and needs no tuned constant; classified once per bake over the zone grid, keyed on world tile coords so chunk and monolithic bakes cannot disagree.
