2026-08-06 merge: `agent/rec-perfect-w2` -> feat/harness-backend (fast-forward to `eb52cf8a`) — EVIDENCE EVERYWHERE, the final workstream of the recommendation perfection campaign (docs/PLAN_REC_PERFECT.md) and the audit's SECOND root cause: `internal:true` starves the generators. An internal reason-only run keeps the caller's system prompt VERBATIM — correct for a strict-format parse, and exactly wrong for the three components that must GUESS what the Commander wants next. The First Pitch (`pitchstore.js`), the goal decomposition (`goalstore.js`) and the ongoing suggestion (`suggeststore.js`) were reasoning from strictly LESS about the Commander than an ordinary task run receives: the static dossier block in their system prompt and nothing else — no learned topics with their verbatim quotes, no open threads, no verdict patterns, no recent activity, no active goal. The runs that need evidence most had the least of it. (1) THE PACK REACHES THEM: a new `evidence:true` flag rides browser (`harness.js`) → route → `runOnce` and appends the SAME bounded, provenance-labelled pack ordinary tasks get (`commander-context.js`, observed-half labelled "weak; never override the current request"). It is APPENDED to the system prompt, never after the directive — the caller's format instruction rides the user message and stays the last thing read. Everything else about the internal path is untouched: no operator manual, no capability summary, no skill catalog, no memory fence, and no recall-stat writes (still gated on `internal` alone, so evidence buys no Memory-Core credit). (2) THE SUGGEST EVIDENCE CONTRACT, in full: the directive now asks for the Commander's OWN words (opt-in `wantEvidence`, so the First Pitch's format contract stays byte-identical), `parsePitch` reads an `EVIDENCE:` line tolerantly (absent or an explicit NONE both read '' — a model admitting it cannot quote them is an HONEST answer), and that quote is VETOED by real token overlap against the station's belief pool (`Autopilot.grounded`/`flattenBeliefs` — the same veto autojobs applies to its GROUNDS line, over a `getBeliefs` accessor added to the shared advice deps so the two channels can never disagree about what the station knows). Fail-CLOSED twice over: no veto engine → no quote; empty pool → no quote, because a check that could not run has not passed. Only a survivor is spoken, in the ONE grammar every other surface uses (`Recommend.whyLine` → «because you said "…"»), and only a survivor is ledgered as real `type:'quote'` evidence — beside the model's own rationale, still typed `rationale` (the W3 law holds; the row now DISTINGUISHES the two, which is what W3's typing fix opened the door to). An ungrounded quote renders nothing and the nudge reads exactly as it did before. (3) THE Q3 STALENESS GUARD the quality-loop plan named but never wired: `UnderstandingStore.probeTarget()` now carries the whole belief record (it was `{dim,text}`, which cannot express an age), and a probe target that reads STALE is DROPPED before the directive is built — the idea goes out un-aimed rather than silently aimed at a memory the station itself would not assert (the arc lane already refuses that; this closes the twin). (4) THE GOAL'S NEXT MILESTONE reaches both generators as a bounded directive fact — the one thing the server pack structurally cannot know, since the milestone tree is decomposed in the browser. DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, recorded rather than left as a silent gap: the plan's `goalAligned` within-band spine term. Nothing in the pass can populate that field, and the quality lane already proved (0 of 20000) what a modifier no candidate populates is worth; the milestone belongs where it changes the OUTPUT, which is the directive. LIVE-PROVEN by a new dev-only prover (`dev/rec-evidence-live.mjs`, 14/14): it drives the REAL sidecar over real HTTP with an in-process mock provider that CAPTURES the system message actually sent — without `evidence:true` the prompt is byte-identical to the caller's (no context block, no goal block, nothing appended); with it the real dossier and the real active goal arrive; and the internal path is still bare of manual/capabilities/skills/memory fence. **2026-08-11 merge digest (WEB_REQUEST CARRIES WORKSPACE FILES — the Etsy/Printify upload wall):** `agent/web-file-body` -> trunk merge `75a835445` -> `83993fac0` (synced onto the moved trunk twice; final merge auto-merged `sidecar/index.js` cleanly, `node --check` + wiring grep verified). User report: a StarNet agent automating an Etsy store could not upload custom mockups to Printify and no workaround existed — root cause was structural: `web_request.body` was model-written TEXT only, so the byte-bearing step of ANY API workflow was impossible at real file sizes (2MB PNG ~ 2.8M base64 chars through context), while the escape hatches (shell curl, browser.upload) sit behind the autonomous exec lockout. Fix mirrors the ${KEY} pattern: the model writes a REFERENCE, the host resolves it at send time, bytes never enter model context in either direction. Two routes: `${file:relative/path}` in the body substitutes host-side base64 (Printify-shape JSON uploads), and a new `multipart` param sends real multipart/form-data (curl -F-shape). Files resolve through the SAME `resolveInside` jail as fs.*/browser.upload (dep wired in index.js); refusals: file refs in url/headers, ${KEY} in body/multipart values, disposition breakouts via quotes/CRLF, 20MB/file + 25MB/request caps; the result label names which files were sent (truthful provenance) and the payload never returns to the model. Boundary rng is injected/crypto (determinism lint caught Math.random on the first gate run — fixed). Teaching seams updated so agents DISCOVER it: tool description + schema, the `<service_keys>` prompt block, and website/docs/connect-a-platform.html (ships with next site deploy). Proof: test/web-request.test.js grew 24->84 assertions (substitution exactness, jail escapes refused pre-send, multipart wire format, caps, nothing-sent-on-refusal); PLUS a live no-mocks wiring probe (real makeFsTools jail + real global fetch): base64 body and multipart file+value round-tripped through httpbin.org and were echoed back intact, cross-workspace escape refused with fs.js''s own error. - 2026-08-15: merged `agent/settings-steady` (pure FF `0371dddbd` -> `f031fe1f4`) — SETTINGS OPENS FAST, AND EVERY CONSOLE HOLDS ONE HEIGHT. Andrew's report: *"in the settings menu its laggier than ever, and windows seem to change size depending on the settings category."* Both were real and both were measured before anything was changed. **THE LAG WAS SIX PICTURES NOBODY ASKED FOR:** `buildSettings` painted all six BACKDROP swatches with the REAL world renderer, inline, on every build of the panel — open, tab swap, or background repaint. Measured live at 112x63 on a seeded station: moon **400ms**, forest **150ms**, nursery 54ms, ocean 26ms, city 14ms, void 9ms — so `openTerm('settings')` cost **501ms** and `rerender('settings')` **405-534ms**, for a pane most opens never scroll to. `Terrain.paintSample` sets `st = null; builtId = ''`, which forces a FULL ground build (patch + overlay + every sprite pool at a 448px reference) per swatch and then throws it away; that is why a thumbnail cost 400ms. Fix in three parts: (1) both layers MEMOISE the chip, keyed `id|w|h|zoom|now` — inputs are fully deterministic (fixed seed `0x0FE57`/`SEED`, no camera, no clock, and grep-verified NO theme coupling: neither module reads `getComputedStyle` or `--ph`), so a cached chip is bit-identical to a fresh render and the swatch is still the real renderer's own pixels, never a stand-in; (2) `mountConsole` grew an optional `sec.onShow(bodyEl)` that fires ONCE when a pane is first revealed — mount, tab click, **or a search, which shows every pane** — so an expensive-and-invisible section costs nothing until it is looked at; (3) APPEARANCE paints one chip per `requestAnimationFrame`, so even the cold pass never blocks a click. ⛔ **THE MOUNT REVEAL MUST BE DEFERRED ONE FRAME** — `onShow` targets are installed by the caller's wiring pass, which runs AFTER `mountConsole` returns, so firing the landing section's hook inline calls a no-op stub and silently skips the one pane the user is looking at. ⛔ **THE BUILDER WAS INNOCENT — INSTRUMENT BEFORE YOU OPTIMISE:** timing every phase of `buildSettings` (10 section fragments, 12 `wireX` passes, `mountConsole`) summed to **3.3ms**, and `toggleTerm`'s phases to ~0; the cost sat in the ~1100 lines of wiring past the last probe. A phase map that says "everything is fast" means your marks miss the slow part, not that it isn't there. **THE RESIZE WAS `.term.console { height: auto }`:** a never-moved window is CSS-centred (`translate(-50%,-50%)`), so a shorter section re-centres the whole box and drags the rail out from under the cursor — measured at 1280x720, SETTINGS was 590 / 534 / 462px across its ten sections. The DOSSIER and DELIVERABLES had each ALREADY been pinned to `--con-h` for exactly this reason, i.e. two per-window exceptions to a default that was wrong for all of them; the shared shell now carries `height: var(--con-h)` and both overrides are deleted. The 2026-08-03 audit that introduced content-fit is not overruled but obsolete — the sparse windows it protected (LOOPS/LOGBOOK/ROUTINES) are no longer windows, they are lanes inside the AUTOMATION console; measured fill after the change is connectors 92%, messaging 92%, automation 99%, agents 278%, so no empty hangars. LIVE PROOF, new `dev/settings-perf-shots.mjs` over CDP in a compositing headless Chrome (**16/16 ok, zero console errors**): open **501ms -> 42-62ms**, rerender **405-534ms -> 5-15ms**, revealing APPEARANCE **~600ms -> 3.7-6.2ms**, a warm repaint of all six swatches **~600ms -> 0.2-0.6ms**, all ten sections **654px with the rail fixed at y=538**, every swatch still painting real content (sampled pixel range 46-112, a blank chip would fail), an overflowing section still scrolling to its end inside the fixed shell, and agents/connectors/messaging/automation/deliverables all holding 654px. ⛔ the preview pane never fires `requestAnimationFrame` (`document.hidden`), so the chunked painter is unobservable there — this had to be driven over CDP. Trunk moved TWICE mid-ritual (overlay-fit + lighting dull, then skin-frame-consistency) — synced INTO the lane each time, `claims.json` the only conflict, regenerated on the synced commit each round (210 files @ `166d5453e`). `frontend/css/app.css` auto-merged against the overlay-fit lane and was hand-verified per the ritual: both sides' markers present exactly once, both dropped rules gone, mirrors byte-identical; `node --check` clean on all three touched JS files with every symbol defined once. - 2026-08-15: merged `agent/black-station` (pure FF `1bd28e7dc` -> `28ea3773a`) — THE STATION MAY NEVER SILENTLY GO BLACK. Andrew, with a screenshot, on shipped 0.10.2: *"there is a DISGUSTING bug on 0.10.2 that I MUST NEVER SEE AGAIN. currently the station randomly went black and the only thing that appears is the agents, and the props."* **THE SYMPTOM NAMED THE CAUSE, once the layers were sorted by HOW THEY ARE DRAWN rather than by module.** Rebuilt every frame: agents (`<img>` sprite sheets) and props (`propsprites.js` creates ZERO canvases — it paints procedurally into the stage ctx). Built ONCE into an offscreen `<canvas>`: the station bake (`stationbake.js` — floors, walls, hull + the lightmap), the sky (`spacebg.js`), the ground (`terrain.js`). The first group survived and the second group was gone — a 1:1 correlation with the draw strategy and with nothing else. **A GPU/driver reset (sleep-wake, a display or DPI change, a TDR, the WebView2 GPU process restarting) zeroes the backing store of every accelerated 2D canvas: the objects survive at full size, the PIXELS do not, and NOTHING THROWS.** So `cache` stayed a well-formed bake and `frameBody` blitted a fully transparent plate every frame; `SpaceBG.draw` still base-filled the ctx directly (spacebg.js:1069), which is why the void read as solid near-black with no stars. `ctx.isContextLost` EXISTS in this WebView — 2D context loss is real here — and nothing was listening for it. **IT COULD NEVER HEAL:** a bake only re-runs when the GEOMETRY changes and no geometry changed, and neither SpaceBG nor Terrain exposed ANY way to drop its built plates, so a blanked sky could not come back for the life of the page. Fix in three parts: (1) `SpaceBG.invalidate()` / `Terrain.invalidate()`, additive — each drops `st` + `builtId` so the next `draw()` re-lays it (Terrain's null also drops the two cached `CanvasPattern`s, which point at the blanked plates); (2) the context events — `'contextlost'` calls `preventDefault()`, which is what ASKS for restoration (without it `'contextrestored'` never fires), and `'contextrestored'` runs the recovery; (3) a WATCHDOG that needs no cooperation from the runtime — one pixel the bake painted OPAQUE, re-read 4x a second, because **alpha is the one property a zeroed backing store cannot fake**. A detected loss rebakes in the SAME frame, so there is no black flash between detect and repaint, and `visibilitychange`/`focus` re-arm the sentinel instantly (a GPU reset usually lands while the app is backgrounded). ⛔⛔ **MY OWN ANTI-THRASH GUARD REINTRODUCED THE BUG, AND ONLY RUNNING THE LIVE PROOF 5x CAUGHT IT:** a flat `now - lastRecoverAt < 3000` cooldown meant the cooldown earned by the FIRST loss made the station sit black through the next one — three of five back-to-back cycles never recovered (14.7% / 10.1% / 11.4% non-black, sentinel still reading blank). **A recovery that restored an opaque bake is PROOF the GPU is healthy, so the next loss must heal on the spot; only a FUTILE recovery — one that changed nothing — is worth rate-limiting.** Never rate-limit the remedy on a timer; rate-limit it on whether it WORKED. ⛔ **RULED OUT WITH ANDREW'S REAL SAVE, not by reasoning:** `StationBake.blankBake` (the 16e6-px guard returning a 1x1 plate) is a perfect-looking match and is unreachable — `TILE=12` x `MAX_SPAN=240` caps the bake at ~8.3M px, and his actual station (`agent.save.json` -> `doc.station`) is 15 rooms / 59 props / 61x35 tiles = a **732x434** bake. A throw in `frameBody` is also ruled out: the crash-guard wrapper leaves the PREVIOUS frame on screen (frozen, not black), and the bake blit precedes the props, so no throw can produce "props but no floor". LIVE PROOF on a seeded worktree sidecar at 808x752, driving one synchronous frame per measurement and histogramming `drawImage(#stage)`: healthy **86.15%** non-black / luma 26.44 -> plates zeroed **15.88%** / luma **6.93** (the reported frame — that residue is precisely props + agents + HUD chrome on a void) -> after the watchdog **86.18%** / luma 26.23. Six back-to-back losses now recover every time (86.00-86.01% against an 86.01% control, 6 recoveries for 6 losses); the `'contextrestored'` path was exercised separately; a clean boot reports **0 recoveries** (no false positives); and the sentinel read costs **0.0023ms**, 0.013% of one frame budget. New `test/canvas-loss-recovery.test.js` (**40 assertions**) source-locks the wiring and **strips comments before matching**, because this fix's own prose names every identifier it asserts — verified to FAIL with 20+ reds against the pre-fix files. Gate on the exact merged tree (pure FF, tree hash-identical to the gated lane tree): `test:fast` **637/637 GREEN FROM THE LOG**, 0 FAIL lines. No `test:http` owed — `sidecar/`, `shared/` and `package.json` are byte-identical across this merge (footprint is frontend + the generated mirror + one test + fast.list + claims). Claims re-locked twice, once per code commit that moved measured bytes (210 files); `npm run sync:website` regenerated `website/app` — the gate locks it byte-exact and went RED on exactly that the first time. **NOT PUSHED** — the diff touches `website/`, and `deploy-website.yml` fires on push for those paths, so pushing auto-deploys starnetos.com; Andrew's call, as with every merge before it. ⛔ **THE FIX REACHES ANDREW ONLY IN A NEW BUILD** — he is running shipped 0.10.2; the instant workaround for a black station is to reload/restart the app, which rebuilds every cache. HONESTLY NOT VERIFIED: the ORIGINAL trigger on his machine was never captured — `startup.log` is the Tauri-side log and carries no browser console, and `EBWebView/Crashpad/reports` was empty. The mechanism is proven and the remedy is cause-agnostic (it heals a blank bake however it got blank), but the specific triggering event is inferred, not observed. The foreign uncommitted Green Guardian auto-refresh row (`2026-08-16 02:33Z @ 70eb70b7`, GREEN) rides with this digest rather than being discarded — it is another session's real telemetry, not this lane's finding.

- 2026-08-16: merged `agent/glyph-speech` (pure FF `fc20cf8a4` -> `38d346bac`) — WHEN TWO AGENTS TALK, YOU CAN SEE THEM TALKING. Andrew: *"when the agents specifically appear to interact with eachother in the simulation a speech bubble pops up above their heads with language that cant be transcripted, like some sort of made up language."* W4/W5 already brought idle bodies together, faced them and made them take turns mouthing; what was missing was the bubble. **THE UNREADABILITY IS THE HONEST REGISTER, NOT A GAG** — a social beat is ambient station LIFE, not a harness event: no message crossed the bus, no run happened, nothing was said, so a bubble of English would be the app asserting content it cannot prove. A script that is not a language asserts only the true part: these two are talking, right now. Words stay in COMMS. So the glyphs are **geometry, not text**: 18 runes, each a stroke list on a 4x6 lattice painted as pixel rects — no font, no codepoint, no string anywhere on the path, so there is literally nothing to copy, paste, translate or screen-read (it also sidesteps the VT323 symbol-glyph fallback entirely and stays crisp at any zoom). Each body draws from an id-seeded 9-of-18 DIALECT, so an agent sounds like itself and a trio reads as three voices rather than one noise source. GATING (verified by grep, not assumption): the only `setTalking(b,true)` in world.js is inside `talkTurn`, which refuses anything that is not a two-sided `huddle`/`border` beat with the body arrived (`pl.holdAt`), and participation needs `socialEligible` -> `bodyIsIdle` — so it fires ONLY for idle agent-to-agent conversation, never from voice/TTS, never while working, never on the silent `watch`/`follow` beats; a real spoken line (`received: …`) always wins the anchor because `drawBubble` is one function and cannot stack two over a head. **THREE BUGS, NONE OF WHICH THE GATE COULD SEE.** (1) ⛔ A LATCH WITH A FIXED DURATION IS THE WRONG SHAPE FOR A TURN-TAKING BEAT — the bubble lived a fixed `speak+fade` from its own stamp, correct only for a body starting exactly on its slot boundary; a body that ARRIVES LATE joins its turn already in progress, so its bubble was still fading ~500ms into the NEXT speaker's and two bubbles were up at once. Found by running the live probe FIVE times (run 5), the same law [[sprite-conversations-lane]] earned. Fixed by anchoring the window to the SLOT (`chatterWindow`, pure + unit-tested): whoever holds turn k is gone at `k*slot+speak+fade` whenever they joined. (2) ⛔ **ANDREW CAUGHT THE ONE I MISSED** — *"it wont repeat the same made up language everytime?"* It did. The seed was `(id, turn)` but the turn index counts from the start of the ENCOUNTER and resets to 0 every time, so every agent replayed ONE identical script in every conversation for the life of the station. The evidence was already in my own probe logs (two separate runs printed byte-identical phrases) and I read past it, because the green "lines CHANGE between turns" check only ever compared WITHIN one encounter — **a freshness check scoped to one session cannot see a cross-session repeat.** Seed is now the turn's ABSOLUTE deadline; locked by a sweep requiring 280+ distinct openings across 300 conversations. (3) the bubble left `fillStyle` on its phosphor and the next frame's 1px motes inherited it (pre-existing in `drawBubble`, but a conversation raises a bubble every 1.7s so it would have become the frame's normal state) — fixed with `save`/`restore` scoped to the chatter path ONLY, so the shipped spoken-line bubble stays byte-identical (golden confirms). **MEASUREMENT TRAPS PAID FOR IN FULL PROBE RUNS:** ⛔⛔ a counter can PASS while the screen DISAGREES — run 1 reported rune ink landing and the captured frame showed no bubble (the spy keyed on `fillStyle` alone and caught foreign motes; the screenshot was taken on the strength of a STATE read while the canvas was a turn behind at 100ms rAF). Drive one synchronous frame yourself (`World.stop(); World.start()`) and measure IN it. ⛔⛔ `drawCurve` barrel-warps AFTER the bubble is drawn, so reading the canvas back at the ink's PRE-WARP rect samples displaced background — measured 4/768 px lit on a bubble plainly visible in the screenshot; read a PADDED region and report tight-vs-wide, the gap IS the warp. ⛔ there is ONE encounter slot, so a probe that FORCES a huddle competes with the idle engine: parked bodies huddle organically within seconds and `_dbgHuddle` then answers "an encounter is already live" forever — ADOPT the organic beat instead of fighting it. LIVE PROOF `dev/glyphprobe.mjs` (`--party 2|3`) asserts bubble<=>talking, never-two-at-once, per-speaker dialects, surviving pixels and zero fillText in the bubble: **pairs 7/7, trios 5/5 conclusive, 0 FAIL ever** (a few trio runs returned INCONCLUSIVE rather than a verdict — that is the single-slot contention, never graded as failure). `dev/glyphdiag.mjs` is the diagnostic that located the ink when the counters lied. Trunk moved 25 commits mid-lane (v0.10.3 train + the comms copy/timestamp lane); synced in, `claims.json` the only conflict both rounds and REGENERATED rather than merged. Gate ON TRUNK after the merge: **test:fast 638/638 green, exit 0, 0 FAIL lines**, `golden` PASS, claims planning PASS (209 files), website mirror synced. NOT PUSHED. NOTE: the Green Guardian's uncommitted STATUS row marks trunk RED at `fc20cf8a` (0 open findings) — that is not `test:fast`, which is green on that base both before and after this lane; its cause is unresolved and belongs to whoever owns that cycle.

- 2026-08-17: merged `agent/sdv-local-colour` (pure FF `0c5e54271` -> `f1e9a9a8c`) — LOCAL COLOUR: THE ART ALREADY HAD THE COLOUR, HALF OF IT NEVER REACHED THE SCREEN. Andrew sent a Stardew Valley interior and asked how to get that look on the asset textures while keeping the space theme, then picked this candidate over a warm-deck one after seeing all three side by side on live local servers. **THE OPENING DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND MEASUREMENT CORRECTED IT.** "The props need more colour" is the obvious answer and it is false: drawn RAW through `PropSprites.setCtx` + `draw` into a scratch canvas, the catalog's lounge/decor family already carries warm oak `#8a6540`, jukebox `#503f20`, sidetable `#63513a`, a deep-red chair and a teal-and-brass couch. Compared against the SAME props' pixels on the live composited canvas over a staged 29-prop room, mean AUTHORED chroma is **28.1/255 and only 13.3 arrives — 52%**; the plants are the extreme (monstera authors 44.4, renders 7.8). So the room reads as grey-green mud not because the palette is grey but because the pipeline eats half of it. **THE CRT PASS IS NOT THE VILLAIN** — scan/fade/vig/grain/aberr all zeroed moved chroma-kept only 52% -> 57% (it costs LUMA, 57% -> 68%). ⛔ **THE LIGHT KNOBS ARE NEARLY INERT ON THEIR OWN**, confirming `stationbake.js`'s own comment from the other direction: even a brutal `ambient` 0.82 -> 0.55, far brighter than Andrew's dialled value and straight into the territory light mode was scrapped over three times, only reached 66%. Also measured and NOT shipped here: the room's DECK is ~60% of its pixels and re-cladding it `OAK`/`PLANK`/`WAINSCOT` — a shipped REFIT choice needing zero code — moved chroma-kept 52% -> 66% in one step and changed the picture more than anything else tried. That candidate is still on the table; Andrew chose the prop-side change. **THE MECHANISM:** `CHROMA` in `propsprites.js` scales the SATURATION of every colour a prop paints, inside `px()` — the file's single paint primitive — holding hue and value exactly, because hue and value are what the silhouette and the projection's lighting logic are built on and saturation is the one axis with no structural job. ⛔ **THE CEILING BINDS, NOT THE MULTIPLIER**: 1.8 and 2.6 land within 1.5 chroma points of each other because the hue-dependent cap does the work. Warm hues (deg <62 or >328 — wood, brass, terracotta, warm fabric) may run to 0.52; **everything else is held at 0.20**, and that low cool cap is the deliberate guard against the 2026-08-16 teal trap, where amplifying a merely-slightly-cool grey turns a casing green on a warm deck. Machinery is supposed to be grey; the defect is a prop with no saturated element anywhere. Already-saturated colour (`s >= 0.45`: emissives, ACC leds, screen phosphor) is left alone, as are the near-black contour and the near-white spec catch. Shipped at **2.6**. ⛔ Checked before merge, not assumed: the boost memoizes by hex string, so a colour derived from `now` would grow that map without bound — there are **zero** `U.shade` calls in the file driven by `now`/`flick`/`Math.sin`/`Math.cos`, every non-constant derivation is a bounded loop index, so the key set is finite. LIVE PROOF, not tests: a 16x12 room furnished with 29 lounge/decor props on a real seeded station, shot through the game's own draw path at camera zoom 2 (an exact integer — a fractional zoom antialiases NN art) and magnified afterwards; on the merged trunk it measures authored **35.31 -> rendered 16.63** against the shipped **28.38 -> 13.34**. on the far edge it reads as a plank STANDING against the wall, the law the turned tables paid for), both shelf boards given 2 rows of top with the books' feet on the FAR edge so the empty front strip of each board reads, a top cap on every spine, the lying stack showing its cover as a 2-row plane over stepped page edges, the plant a crown splayed round a pot RIM. **fishtank** — the water SURFACE is now the subject (6 rows of plan view), the front glass drops 12 rows -> 4 (the minor face) and reads through one bold specular WEDGE, and the hood becomes a bar along the north rim instead of a lid that hides the plane the projection exists to show. ⛔ **A TURN TOWARD PLAN VIEW IS A VALUE PROBLEM, NOT JUST A GEOMETRY ONE.** Three consequences, each caught by rendering not by reasoning: a mid-grey water plane between a mid-grey hood and a mid-grey cabinet is three STRIPES rather than an object (the water was darkened and the stand pushed under it); a lit near rim splits the tank into two stacked windows (it is a thin steel frame, and a broken dashed meniscus in its place was worse — noise); and the plan view exposed how much scatter the elevation had been hiding — gravel mottle + a ripple net + caustics spread over the whole surface + 3 fish + a bubbler turned the water into confetti, so the bed became ONE band along the near edge and the caustics were held to the tube's own rows. ⛔ **A FULL-WIDTH ROW DRAWN OVER A CHAMFERED CONTOUR LEAVES A LIT CORNER OUTSIDE THE OUTLINE** and the whole top plane then reads as a lid laid on top; the far row is inset 1px on both props. ⛔ **ONE HOT PIXEL IS NOT A WEST RAIL, IT IS A SPECK** — a warm `keyEdge` on the cold end of the cold prop had to go. LIVE PROOF `dev/propangle-live-proof.mjs` (new), on a seeded sidecar over CDP, both props placed through the REAL mutation API (`Build.__test__.station().addProp`): it A/Bs against the art at a PINNED baseline commit loaded into the same page under shoot.html's module shim, so both builds are measured by identical code on identical canvases — **bookshelf top-plane rows 2 -> 5** (consecutive rows that are >=80%% lit timber: a crown line scores 2, a surface scores 5) and **fishtank distinct fish rows 1 -> 4** (in an elevation a fish can only travel left-right, so it is pinned to one row; from above it drifts in TWO axes — an integer that shading cannot fake). Both props located on the real stage canvas by their own signature colour, **zero console errors, 5/5 runs PASS**. ⛔ the first two probe designs were thrown away: a predicted canvas box misses by a tile because the composited frame is warped and panned (`dev/floorseam-live.mjs` already knew this) — SEARCH the neighbourhood and take the peak, never predict; and a single-column luma profile through a bookcase hits books, gaps and boards and measures nothing. `gal/shoot.html` gained `?crop=1` so a tall zoom still fits in a reviewable image without resampling. Gate on the exact merged tree: `test:fast` **647/647 GREEN FROM THE LOG**, exit 0. No `test:http` owed — `sidecar/`, `shared/` and `package.json` are untouched (footprint is `frontend/app/propsprites.js` + the generated mirror + the dev harness + claims). `npm run sync:website` regenerated `website/app` — the gate went RED on exactly that the first time, as it always does. Claims re-locked twice, once in the lane and once on trunk after the merge (209 files). **NOT PUSHED** — the diff touches `website/`, and `deploy-website.yml` fires on push for those paths; Andrew's call, as with every merge before it. - 2026-08-17: merged `agent/tank-gravel` (merge `a13ac13fa` + `4e6dd0d` -> `70138391f`, relock `166ee8aa3`) â€” THE FISH TANK READS AS A FISH TANK, AND THE RACK AND THE STUDIO GET A TOP. The follow-on to the eye-level projection lane, driven entirely by Andrew reading the renders, and it cost four wrong answers before the right one. â›”â›”â›” **A PLAN VIEW OF A TANK IS A PUDDLE.** The first fix over-corrected the elevation into an almost pure plan â€” ten rows of water surface over a three-row sliver of glass â€” and his verdict was that it looked weird and made no sense. He is right, and the general law is the useful part: **a GLASS BOX at a 3/4 camera shows BOTH of its faces, and the content belongs in the TALLER one.** The tank is now a foreshortened SURFACE PLANE across the top (that is the 3/4, and it is what the shipped v4 had none of) over the WATER COLUMN seen through the near glass â€” gravel on the floor, plants rooted in it, a castle standing on it, fish in SIDE view, which is the picture anyone recognises as an aquarium and which is honest here because the near wall is glass. Three separate wrong reads were paid for on the way, each one a law: â›”â›”â›” **GRAVEL IS THE FLOOR, SO IN PLAN IT IS THE WHOLE PICTURE AND NEVER A BAND** â€” a bed laid along the near edge (reasoning that a tank's floor slopes up toward the viewer) read as *"a patch of dirt in the middle of it... the dirt would be at the BOTTOM of the fucking tank"*, and the deeper point is that **in a plan view there is no bottom-of-the-picture to put a floor at**, which is itself the argument for the column carrying the content. â›”â›”â›” **A STEEL RAIL BETWEEN TWO WATER ZONES CUTS THE PROP IN HALF** â€” *"why is it cut off in the middle?"* Three faults, one symptom: a hard divider, a hue break (blue pane against a gravel-green plan) and a SECOND gravel bed inside the pane. There is no rail now; one ramp runs the whole body of water and the waterline is the only marker, which is a real feature of a tank rather than a seam. â›”â›”â›” **AUTHOR THE WATER RAMP, DO NOT `U.shade()` ONE UP** â€” shade() desaturates as it lightens (the same trap the poker table's pedestal hit), so the part of the tank the tube lights came out PALE GREY and Andrew read it, correctly, as *"ITS MISSING THE TOP PORTION, ITS COLORED GRAY INDICATING THERE IS NOT ENOUGH WATER"*. Both ends of the ramp are authored constants now and the tube's bloom was cut from 0.32 to 0.16 because **a fat bloom on the rim bleaches the top of the water**, which is the same defect arriving by a different route. Also â›” **THE WATER IS THE BRIGHTEST THING ON THE PROP** â€” an earlier pass held it dark on the theory that a mid-value plane between hood and cabinet reads as three stripes, and got *"it looks like all the water was taken out of the tank"*: a lit aquarium is a BACKLIT object and is supposed to glow. FISH rebuilt: â›” **two coloured pixels is a pellet, not a fish** â€” the read is the taper (head, two-row body, peduncle, forked caudal), a dorsal fin, an eye, a tail that beats on its own fast clock independent of the lane drift, and three different SIZES; and â›” **against cyan water the readable fish are WARM or PALE** (the teal one sat on the water's own hue and vanished; gold/coral/silver now). **shelf** â€” 38 rows -> 26 and the same projection fix: the cap is a five-row top plane keyed down its WEST rail, both boards show two rows of top surface with the contents standing on the far edge, and every case, canister, drive and cartridge carries a lit top. Binders were tried here and CUT on Andrew's call â€” coloured book spines turn a bolted equipment rack into library furniture. **studio** â€” had no top at all; it gains a five-row top DECK with the output tray recessed into it (a printer's top IS a tray, so nothing was invented) and the preview panel becomes a RAKED TRAPEZOID â€” narrow at the far edge, wide at the near one â€” because â›” **a rectangle facing the camera is an elevation and a trapezoid is a plane tilted toward you**; height, lens, CMY channels and print slot unchanged. **bar / beanbag** â€” every animated light removed on request: the under-counter accent no longer breathes, the shelf pilot lamp no longer blinks, the pour glint and the beanbag's satin glint are deleted (the beanbag is now fully static). The tap DRIP is still there â€” it is a drip, not a light. â›” **A CATALOG-WIDE SCAN IS CHEAP AND WORTH DOING ONCE**: all 119 props rendered as contact sheets through `gal/shoot.mjs` at the game's camera scale found exactly five more elevations still standing â€” `trophycase` (1px shelf boards, no top plane, the pre-fix bookshelf exactly), `pinball` (a front view of a cabinet whose PLAYFIELD should be the top plane, which `quarters_pooltable` already does correctly), `bunk` (head-on bed; the mattress top is the subject), `terrarium` (a flat glass box, the fish tank's family) and `bookstack` (spines side-on, no top cover plane). Recorded, deliberately NOT touched â€” Andrew scoped this lane to the shelf and the studio. Tooling: `gal/shoot.html` gained `?crop=1` in the earlier lane and it is what made the scan reviewable; â›” **keep a contact sheet under 2000px wide or the reviewer sees a downscaled blur and cannot judge pixels at all.** Gate on the exact merged tree: `test:fast` **647/647 GREEN FROM THE LOG**, exit 0. ## 2026-08-22 — dead-end screens lane → trunk `29f042719` (merge `89f1ac37e`) — fast 680/680 · http 83/83
Two real users stranded on the same day, two dead-end screens, one root cause class: a gate with no exit.
- `sidecar/workspace-owner.js`: a claim stamped BEFORE the current OS boot is provably dead (PIDs reset at boot; kill(0) on a reused PID said "busy" forever → every spawn exited before listening → STATION DATA UNREACHABLE with no way out). Torn lock predating boot also reclaims. Opt-in via `makeBootedAt(now)`; same-boot live PID still busy.
- UNREACHABLE screen: `starnet_restart_sidecar` shell command (kill + respawn, truthful listening bool), RESTART STATION SERVICE button (hidden in browser mode), one automatic restart after ~30s of failed polls. Desktop path proved by `cargo check` only — not live on a Mac.
- PRIOR STATION DATA FOUND: START FRESH (two-press) → `POST /api/lineage/start-fresh` moves current-workspace state to a sibling `workspace-quarantine/<stamp>/` (never deletes), acknowledges legacy/snapshot roots via `.fresh-start.json`, exits 75 → clean onboarding. Live-proved over CDP + full HTTP restart test; legacy saves byte-exact.
- Connect screen: a linked StarNet account with $0 says so (ADD CREDITS, 10s balance poll flips green), WAKE refuses up front; billing refusals named as billing. Also fixed: `preflightWire` read only `res.text`, so EVERY up-front refusal showed "the provider returned an error" — the real reason never reached the screen.
Laws: a lock must distinguish "PID alive" from "my process alive" · a gate owes an exit that cannot fail · a refusal string that never reaches the screen is a fail-open.
